advanced_moves.action: Place CL 1B before the EQ pair, use ME 1B for placement and PE 1C for outer contour, then compare Mk I/Mk II at equal reduction.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Compression stays stable while EQ reshapes the result; judge generation on movement, not gain.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Compressor-first keeps both EQs out of its main detector decision.

advanced_moves.setup: A stereo master has center congestion but attractive side air.
advanced_moves.action: Enable M/S, unlink, reduce Mid with ME 1B and light CL 1B, leave Side air, then adjust Parallel Compression.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Center clears without narrowing; parallel changes compression only.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Mk II gives independent M/S sets, and Dry/Wet blends only CL 1B.

use_cases.application: Control first, place mids with ME 1B, add broad PE 1C contour afterward.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Three licensed stages divide vocal tasks more explicitly than one console strip.

use_cases.application: Use restrained independent M/S EQ and optical compression while preserving side ambience.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: M/S routing and broad tube curves offer inspectable character without a digital multiband chain.

insider_note: Documented: Parallel Compression affects CL 1B only; both EQs remain fully applied, and neither affects external sidechain.
avoid_when: Avoid it for narrow surgical cuts, dynamic EQ, or true-peak delivery; its strength is broad contour and optical control.

sources.title: Softube Tube-Tech Classic Channel and Classic Channel Mk II user manual

name: Chandler Zener-Bender
comparative_edge: Choose it over Zener-Bender for Console 1 when native dual-channel panels, order reversal, channel linking, and full M/S matter. Choose Tube-Tech Classic Channel for optical smoothness. Chandler's edge is broad Curve Bender tone interacting with Zener modes and THD in either order.

advanced_moves.setup: A broad top lift makes limiting too aggressive.
advanced_moves.action: Start Zener before Curve Bender, establish dynamics, reverse order with same EQ, then lower Zener input to match reduction.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Limiter-first keeps movement steadier; EQ-first makes top boost join detection and drive.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The switch physically reverses order, changing spectrum and level entering Zener.

advanced_moves.setup: A wide drum or guitar bus needs side color but center compression.
advanced_moves.action: Enable M/S, unlink Zener, compress Mid in Comp 1, use Side THD or lighter reduction, then balance EQ.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Center tightens while sides grow without image drift or hollow mono.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Both units support M/S, and unlinking gives independent dynamics.

use_cases.application: Compare order so Curve Bender boosts either provoke or follow Zener compression.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The routable pairing makes tone-to-dynamics interaction a deliberate choice.

use_cases.application: Use independent M/S Zener modes and broad EQ to anchor center while enlarging sides.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Native M/S panels offer more spatial authorship than Console 1 adaptation.

insider_note: Documented: linked compression shares gain reduction, not just knobs. Link heavier stereo reduction; unlink for true M/S.
avoid_when: Avoid it when rapid per-channel strip work matters more than routing depth; use the Console 1 version.

sources.title: Softube Chandler Limited Zener-Bender user manual

name: Chandler Zener-Bender for Console 1
comparative_edge: Choose it over native Zener-Bender when fast channel-strip mapping matters more than dual-panel routing. It condenses Curve Bender and Zener into EQ, Compressor, and Drive, with low-gain 0.5 dB precision expanding to ±15 dB. Native remains better for order reversal and detailed M/S.

advanced_moves.setup: Move from mastering-scale EQ into one assertive channel move.
advanced_moves.action: Keep most bands in sub-5 dB fine steps, then push only the needed band into the wider mixing range.
advanced_moves.listen_for: One band becomes the effect while others retain finishing precision.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Softube merged ±5 and ±15 dB gain laws with amount-dependent resolution.

advanced_moves.setup: Add Zener color to a vocal without reduction.
advanced_moves.action: Bypass Compressor, set Drive around noon, sweep Character around neutral, level-match, then add EQ.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Upper-mid distortion rises clockwise and cleans counterclockwise without EQ hiding excess.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Drive is separate Zener THD; Character changes upper-mid emphasis.

use_cases.application: Use THD Drive for presence, then make low-gain Curve Bender moves without compression.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Separate Drive and adaptive EQ gain law deploy Chandler color faster than native panels.

use_cases.application: Use Comp 1 with low-gain EQ moves from Console 1 hardware.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Mapping prioritizes tactile recall over native routing depth.

insider_note: Documented: Zener input/output becomes one Threshold without changing modeled operation. Shape is empty and falls back to Core, not Chandler circuitry.
avoid_when: Avoid it when order switching or full dual-channel M/S controls are required; use native Zener-Bender.

sources.title: Softube Chandler Limited Zener-Bender for Console 1 user manual

name: Empirical Labs Trak Pak for Console 1
comparative_edge: Choose it over American Class A when high-frequency limiting/de-essing and Mike-E compression/saturation matter more than a gate and stepped-console workflow. Choose Weiss Gambit for cleaner digital control. Trak Pak separates harshness control, compression, and CompSat-style color into tactile sections.

advanced_moves.setup: A bright bus turns harsh only in dense passages.
advanced_moves.action: Set Shape to HF Limiter, place its crossover near the harshness, adjust for pileups only, then add Drive separately after confirming the high-frequency control.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Highs integrate on dense moments without permanent shelf dulling.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: HF Limiter dynamically controls above crossover while Mike-E saturation remains separate.

advanced_moves.setup: A bus compressor should keep transients but gain density.
advanced_moves.action: Use low ratio, slowest attack, fast release, 1–3 dB reduction, then add Drive separately and sweep Character.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Attacks pass while body controls; extra density comes from Drive, not deeper reduction.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The strip separates Mike-E compression from Warm/Toasty distortion.

use_cases.application: Use HF Limiter for dense fizz, Lil FrEQ mids for placement, and Mike-E Drive for weight.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It handles dynamic harshness and saturation separately, avoiding static high cuts.

use_cases.application: Use slow-attack Mike-E compression and Warm/Toasty Drive for density.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Compression/saturation split is more controllable than American Class A Punchy alone.

insider_note: Documented: Shape is Lil FrEQ de-esser/HF limiter, not a gate. HF Limiter affects every frequency above crossover.
avoid_when: Avoid it for below-threshold cleanup, M/S, or transparent limiter output; Weiss Gambit is better aligned.

sources.title: Softube Empirical Labs Trak Pak user manual

name: Weiss Gambit Series for Console 1
comparative_edge: Choose it over colored strips when below-threshold control, surgical EQ1 bands, and DS1-derived limiting should stay clean. Choose Weiss Compressor/Limiter outside Console 1 for deeper above-threshold work. Gambit's edge is below-threshold compression that raises quiet detail without pushing down attacks.

advanced_moves.setup: A drum room or reverb tail needs detail without flattened direct hits.
advanced_moves.action: Choose 1:x below-threshold compression, set Threshold below hits, and constrain Range until ambience rises without noise.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Tails become continuous while direct transients remain; rising hiss means Range is too broad.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Below-threshold compression raises quiet material, and Range caps the change.

advanced_moves.setup: Use Gambit EQ/compressor during tracking without limiter latency.
advanced_moves.action: Load Gambit EQ or Compressor into another strip, replace Drive with low-latency output, and reserve full Gambit for playback.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Monitoring improves without EQ/compressor tone changing.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The limiter is the main latency source and sections are independently loadable.

use_cases.application: Use range-limited below-threshold compression to reveal decays without touching hits.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: No other Softube strip exposes this DS1-derived behavior directly in Shape.

use_cases.application: Use EQ1-derived cuts and DS1 compression while replacing the limiter during monitoring.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Clean sections avoid console color and can be separated from latency-heavy output.

insider_note: Documented: Drive is a DS1/MM-1 limiter. Below noon lowers ceiling; above noon adds gain into a 0 dB ceiling. Character selects limiter type.
avoid_when: Avoid the full strip during latency-sensitive tracking unless limiter is replaced; avoid quiet-detail lifting on noisy sources without tight Range.

sources.title: Softube Weiss Gambit Series user manual

name: Tape
comparative_edge: Choose Tape over Dirty Tape for controllable machine family, speed, crosstalk, and mastering-scale cohesion rather than overt damage. Choose Harmonics when transient reconstruction and distortion family matter more than tape motion; choose Overstayer M-A-S when peak bending without wow, noise, or tape bandwidth is the goal.

advanced_moves.setup: On a bus, set 15 or 30 ips, disable Noise, Stability modulation, and Crosstalk, then switch the VU meters to THD.
advanced_moves.action: For each Type, adjust Input and Amount to the same subtle THD reading and match Output before comparing. Add HF Trim only after selecting the machine behavior.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Compare transient rounding, low-frequency contour, and sustain at equal distortion and loudness; reject a type that wins only because it is hotter.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The three tape types are input-dependent, and both Input and Amount change their color; matching THD and loudness reduces drive-level bias without pretending the harmonic spectra are identical.

advanced_moves.setup: On a stereo pad, echo, or backing-vocal return, select a stable Type and set Dry/Wet below full.
advanced_moves.action: Reduce Speed Stability until modulation becomes audible, then adjust Dry/Wet for deliberate chorus depth. Add Crosstalk separately and re-check mono before touching HF Trim.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Pitch motion should enlarge the return without pulling the dry center off pitch; mono should not reveal phasey thinning.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Blending dry with a speed-varying tape path creates chorusing, while Crosstalk adds a separate left/right leakage mechanism.

use_cases.application: Compare Types at equal THD and output, use a higher speed for restrained transient control, then compensate only the high-frequency loss that remains.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Tape exposes machine family, speed, THD, and HF compensation directly; Dirty Tape bundles those concerns into a degradation effect.

use_cases.application: Use partial Dry/Wet with slight instability for ensemble spread, then add restrained crosstalk and check mono.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its separately adjustable motion and stereo leakage can make a clean return feel recorded together without the overt dropouts of Dirty Tape.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Tape.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Tape
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Dry/Wet combined with Speed Stability can create chorusing. Crosstalk in Studio One Mix FX controls leakage across session channels, not only within one stereo insert.
avoid_when: Avoid it when the production needs obvious dropouts or decoupled damage—use Dirty Tape—or when timing modulation must be absent but peak density is wanted—use Overstayer M-A-S.

name: Dirty Tape
comparative_edge: Choose Dirty Tape over Tape when wow, flutter, dropouts, darker low-speed color, and channel-to-channel instability are arrangement elements. Choose Tape for separable speed, crosstalk, noise, and machine types; choose OTO Biscuit for clocked digital reduction or Bad Speaker for a physical playback perspective.

advanced_moves.setup: On a static loop, set Dirt to minimum, Stereo Mode to Normal, and match Output before raising Drive.
advanced_moves.action: Find the distortion density with Drive alone, then return Drive slightly and raise Dirt until mechanical motion contributes as much as the saturation. Re-match after each stage.
advanced_moves.listen_for: You should be able to identify harmonic thickening and transport damage as two separate contributions; stop when dropouts erase the loop's groove anchor.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Drive increases tape distortion, while Dirt is a macro for wow, flutter, dropouts, crosstalk, and lower-speed coloration.

advanced_moves.setup: On a stereo effects return rather than the dry source, switch from Normal to De-coupled after setting a moderate Dirt amount.
advanced_moves.action: Automate Dirt into transitions and compare coupled versus independent channel variation. Narrow the return downstream if the center wanders too far.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The return should breathe wider at transitions while the dry signal preserves pitch and center; avoid random image jumps on featured notes.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: De-coupled mode allows wow, flutter, and dropout variations to differ between left and right channels.

use_cases.application: Build distortion with Drive, introduce Dirt separately for motion, and keep the dry keys outside the insert so note attacks remain stable.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its two macros separate nonlinear density from compound mechanical wear more clearly than a generic lo-fi preset.

use_cases.application: Automate De-coupled Dirt upward across a transition while lowering the high cut, then return abruptly to a stable dry scene.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Independent-channel transport defects create temporal and spatial deterioration that Bad Speaker's static device responses do not.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Dirt at maximum also applies coloration associated with low tape speed; at minimum it corresponds to high speed. It is not a modulation-depth control with otherwise constant tone.
avoid_when: Avoid it for subtle mastering glue, separately tuned crosstalk/noise, or repeatable wow rate; Tape exposes those decisions more cleanly.

name: Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor
comparative_edge: Choose Harmonics over Saturation Knob when the nonlinear family, pre-emphasis, filters, blend, and post-distortion dynamics need separate control. Choose Overstayer M-A-S for hardware-specific peak bending and emphasis profiles, or Weiss Exciter when additive, frequency-targeted harmonics with minimal fundamental/EQ change are the priority.

advanced_moves.setup: On a kick, choose the least intrusive Drive Type, leave Drive at minimum or near-minimum, switch Dynamics on, and level-match the plug-in output.
advanced_moves.action: Treat Dynamics as the main processor: move it counterclockwise for a denser, rounder hit or clockwise for more front-edge separation. Only add Drive afterward if the kick actually needs overt saturation.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Counterclockwise should pull body and low-level detail forward like colorful compression; clockwise should make the attack separate without the click becoming detached.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Dynamics analyzes the waveform before distortion and reconstructs or suppresses its movement, so the control can behave like a colored compressor/expander even when saturation is not the goal.

advanced_moves.setup: For a full-range source, duplicate Harmonics in series at low drive rather than pushing one full-band instance.
advanced_moves.action: Use the first instance's filters and Character to color the lower region with one Type, and the second to treat the upper region with another. Match each stage before judging the chain.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Low and high regions should acquire distinct textures without a single shared clipping ceiling flattening the whole source.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Each Drive Type has tailored pre-distortion Character filtering, and serial low-drive stages can generate different harmonic structures in different spectral regions.

use_cases.application: Keep Drive at minimum or near-minimum and use Dynamics alone as a one-knob colored transient shaper: left for density and weight, right for greater attack contrast.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its pre-distortion envelope analysis gives a different, more nonlinear-feeling result than a conventional attack/sustain shaper.

use_cases.application: Use Character to focus drive on the useful register, then restore clocked attack with clockwise Dynamics rather than simply lowering Drive.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its dynamics reconstruction separates transient preservation from harmonic density, which Saturation Knob cannot.

use_cases.application: Treat lower and upper bands with two low-drive instances using different Types, preserving pick attack on the upper stage with Dynamics.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Multiple nonlinear families, filters, and reconstruction allow controlled division of weight and grind without a separate multiband saturator.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Producer practice: the catalog's sleeper move is to ignore overt saturation and use Dynamics as a colorful compressor/expander, especially on kicks. Softube documents the pre-distortion analysis and envelope reconstruction; the Drive-minimum application is a producer technique, not an official preset recipe.
avoid_when: Avoid it when one protected-band macro is enough—Saturation Knob is faster—or when the goal is only newly generated, precisely targeted harmonics—use Weiss Exciter.

sources.title: Softube Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor user manual
Bobby Owsinski: Softube Harmonics production review

name: Saturation Knob
comparative_edge: Choose it over Harmonics when speed and one protected spectral extreme are more valuable than choosing a distortion family or rebuilding dynamics. Choose Harmonics for filters, Character, Dry/Wet, THD metering, and transient control; choose Overstayer M-A-S when subtle peak bending with auto gain is the job.

advanced_moves.setup: On a bass source, duplicate to a parallel bus, high-pass that bus if the host permits, and set Saturation Knob to Keep Low.
advanced_moves.action: Drive until upper harmonics make the bass readable on small speakers, then blend under the clean track and verify the fundamental in mono.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Pitch should translate at low playback level while the original sub envelope remains stable; stop if the parallel path produces fizzy note edges.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Keep Low applies more saturation to higher frequencies, preserving the lower region relative to Neutral mode.

advanced_moves.setup: On bright percussion, set Keep High and begin from no saturation with output matched downstream.
advanced_moves.action: Raise the knob until snare or body thickens beneath the cymbal band, then automate bypass for sections that need unprocessed transient contrast.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Lower percussion body should gain density while hats retain definition; reject settings that turn the complete bus dull.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Keep High biases saturation toward lower frequencies so the high-frequency material remains comparatively intact.

use_cases.application: Use Keep High to densify kick and snare beneath cymbals, then blend the bus rather than driving the full kit insert.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The three-position spectral bias reaches a useful protected-top parallel sound faster than configuring Harmonics.

use_cases.application: Use Neutral as a waveshaper to introduce harmonics, then control the resulting brightness with a later filter or the arrangement.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its simple clipping stage can turn spectrally sparse waveforms into audible overtone material without tape motion or speaker coloration.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Saturation Knob.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Saturation Knob
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the labels describe what is preserved. Keep Low saturates the higher portion more; Keep High saturates the lower portion more. Reading them as the processed band reverses the intended choice.
avoid_when: Avoid it when precise level matching, blend, filtering, or transient recovery must live inside the plugin; Harmonics supplies those controls.

sources.title: Softube Saturation Knob for Modular user manual

name: Overstayer M-A-S
comparative_edge: Choose standard M-A-S over Extended when six musically constrained emphasis profiles are faster than drawing a four-band emphasis curve. Choose Extended for exact spectral targeting; choose Harmonics for multiple analog-family models and dynamics reconstruction, or Tape when speed, crosstalk, and transport behavior are part of the sound.

advanced_moves.setup: On a track or bus, enable Auto Gain, set Mix fully wet, choose Classic M-A-S, and raise Input until the first saturation LED responds.
advanced_moves.action: Cycle all six Emphasis Types, re-adjusting Input each time to equalize the amount of saturation before selecting by tone. Restore parallel balance only after choosing.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Judge which region bends first and how steady versus transient material reacts; reject a mode that wins only because it is driven harder.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Emphasis changes the operating range and frequency weighting before the M-A-S stages, so equal Input settings do not create equal saturation.

advanced_moves.setup: On a vocal or bright instrument that dulls as peaks bend, establish the desired Input and Mix with Dual and 2nd off.
advanced_moves.action: Engage Dual, then 2nd separately, retaining the smallest addition that restores clarity. Revisit Emphasis Type before adding top EQ downstream.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Presence should return as harmonic energy without sibilance becoming brittle or the fundamental losing weight.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Dual and 2nd add more second harmonics and brighten the distorted result rather than applying a conventional high-frequency boost.

use_cases.context: Dance pop — Drum and instrument buses
use_cases.application: Use low-drive M-A-S across several buses with source-specific Emphasis Types, re-matching Input whenever the type changes.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The standard profiles make cumulative peak bending faster to distribute than building a custom Extended curve on every bus.

use_cases.application: Compare Classic and Bass Distortion at equal LED activity, then add Dual only if the bent bass loses audibility above the fundamental.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its emphasis profiles decide which spectral regions clip while the broad M-A-S operating range can bend peaks without compressor release motion.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Overstayer M-A-S.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Overstayer M-A-S
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the first meter LED marks where bending begins, but low-order harmonic color exists below that point. 'No LED' is not necessarily a null-processing state.
avoid_when: Avoid standard M-A-S when a specific emphasis frequency or cutoff must be set; use M-A-S Extended. Avoid it for time instability or tape noise.

name: Overstayer M-A-S Extended
comparative_edge: Choose Extended over standard M-A-S when the saturation must be aimed at exact regions with a four-band emphasis EQ and resonant pre-filters. Choose standard for faster repeatable profiles across many tracks; choose Drawmer 1976 when saturation and stereo width must be independently controlled in three explicit crossover bands.

advanced_moves.setup: On a full-range bus, enable Emphasis, set filters wide, Auto Gain on, disengage Compensation for the target band, and establish low-level bending with Input before moving the EQ.
advanced_moves.action: Boost the pre-emphasis band feeding the target into saturation, then adjust its independent outer-ring post control toward the original tonal balance. Compare with the same apparent EQ but less Input.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The target region should gain harmonic density while the final broad spectrum stays close to bypass; reject a move that is only audible as EQ.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Extended exposes the pre/post emphasis shaping that the standard version packages into fixed profiles, separating what drives from what is heard after.

advanced_moves.setup: For a bass-heavy or harsh source, engage only the pre-saturation HPF or LPF with resonance at minimum.
advanced_moves.action: Move the cutoff until the vulnerable extreme stops driving the stage, then add only enough Resonance to restore energy at the boundary. Re-set Input after filtering.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The protected extreme should stay cleaner while the cutoff area remains connected; stop if resonance becomes a new note or whistle.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The 12 dB/octave resonant filters precede saturation, changing both the driven spectrum and the harmonics subsequently generated.

use_cases.application: Use pre/post emphasis to make the middle distort while returning lows and highs near the original balance, then blend beneath the clean mix.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It offers continuous control over the spectral drive/de-emphasis relationship that standard M-A-S only approximates with profiles.

use_cases.application: High-pass before saturation, emphasize a chosen presence zone, and use filter resonance sparingly to keep the effect voiced around the singer.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The pre-saturation filters and editable emphasis can isolate vocal color more precisely than Harmonics' global Character control.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the hardware's emergency op-amp safety-clipping circuit was deliberately omitted from both plug-ins after consultation with Overstayer. Very hot digital input can therefore reach a different final failure mode than the hardware.
avoid_when: Avoid Extended when one of the six standard profiles already fits; its extra pre/post and resonant controls add ways to mis-level the comparison.

name: Drawmer 1976 Three Band Saturator
comparative_edge: Choose Drawmer 1976 over Harmonics when the production decision is explicitly low/mid/high saturation plus independent stereo width. Choose Harmonics for nonlinear families and transient reconstruction without crossovers; choose M-A-S Extended for continuous pre/post emphasis and peak bending rather than three recombined bands.

advanced_moves.setup: On a full mix or drum-and-bass bus, set both crossovers around musical role boundaries, all Width controls centered, and Mono Check available.
advanced_moves.action: Keep Low Width at or near mono, widen Mid and High in separate passes, then toggle Mono Check after each. Add saturation only after the stereo architecture translates.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Sub energy and the phantom center should remain fixed while upper ambience expands; mono should preserve impact rather than exposing a scooped band.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Each crossover band has independent width before recombination, so stereo expansion can be limited to regions that tolerate side energy.

advanced_moves.setup: For a source whose midrange needs density but whose extremes are already controlled, bypass or zero all three saturators and set crossovers by soloed musical roles.
advanced_moves.action: Drive Mid first, then add smaller Low or High amounts only if the recombined source feels disconnected. Revisit crossovers after saturation because generated harmonics may cross the chosen boundaries.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Mid density should increase without a seam at either crossover or a softer sub transient.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The signal is split before three independent nonlinear stages, so crossover placement decides which fundamentals generate harmonics in each processor.

use_cases.context: Drum and bass — Bass and drum master bus
use_cases.application: Keep the low band narrow and lightly driven, saturate the mid growl, and widen only upper bands while checking mono.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its three parallel width and saturation zones protect sub localization more directly than a full-band saturator.

use_cases.context: Orchestral trailer — Percussion and low-brass stem
use_cases.application: Use light low/mid saturation for scale, leaving high saturation restrained while widening only the upper room contribution.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Frequency-specific density and width can enlarge a composite stem without putting cymbal air and low impacts through the same nonlinear stage.

insider_note: Engineering inference from the documented split-band architecture: crossover changes after drive is set alter not only band level but which fundamentals feed each nonlinear stage, so always re-evaluate saturation after moving a crossover.
avoid_when: Avoid it when crossover phase/partitioning is undesirable or when one continuous full-band transfer curve is the goal; use Harmonics or Overstayer M-A-S.

sources.title: Softube Drawmer 1976 Three Band Saturator user manual
Softube Drawmer 1976 Three Band Saturator product page

name: OTO Biscuit 8-bit Effects
comparative_edge: Choose Biscuit over Dirty Tape for clock-rate reduction, individual bit mutation, a multimode analog-modeled filter, and tempo-capable digital effects. Choose Dirty Tape for continuous mechanical instability, or Bad Speaker when the illusion should be a physical playback device rather than exposed data conversion.

advanced_moves.setup: Set all eight bits on, Brain off, Naked at unity, Dressed low, and Clock high enough that the source remains recognizable.
advanced_moves.action: Mute or invert LSBs one at a time before touching higher bits; lower Clock only after a useful bit pattern emerges. Keep a limiter or conservative monitoring level downstream.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Low-order changes should add texture while preserving rhythm and pitch; stop before an MSB change creates uncontrolled level or replaces the source with static.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: LSBs create subtler changes than MSBs, whose inversion or removal radically changes the 8-bit sample value and can produce loud noise.

advanced_moves.setup: On a drum fill or synth sequence, establish the core bit/Clock sound, engage Brain's Step effect, and tempo-reference the pattern.
advanced_moves.action: Sequence filter movement while using the analog-modeled multimode Filter for the final bandwidth. Blend Naked and Dressed rather than filtering the dry path externally.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Rhythmic degradation should reinforce the phrase grid while transients remain locatable in the dry component.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: One Brain effect can run alongside sample-rate reduction and bit mutation, followed by a resonant low-, band-, or high-pass filter and parallel mixer.

use_cases.application: Develop an LSB-first bit pattern, lower Clock for bandwidth, then animate the Step filter for one resampled transition.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It combines data-level mutation, clock artifacts, rhythmic effect, and analog-style filtering in one repeatable digital instrument.

use_cases.application: Blend Dressed beneath Naked, automate one or two bit inversions, and use Pitch as the single active Brain effect for phrase-end mutations.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Individual bit states create discrete timbral events that Dirty Tape's continuous Dirt macro cannot reproduce.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the bit switches have three states—on, muted, and inverted—and the most significant bit is the most drastic. Shift-click changes all switches to the same state, which can cause an abrupt full-pattern jump.
avoid_when: Avoid it on uncontrolled full-level masters or when smooth analog degradation is required; bit inversions can be very loud, and Dirty Tape is the safer continuous-motion choice.

sources.title: Softube OTO Biscuit 8-bit Effects user manual

name: Bad Speaker
comparative_edge: Choose Bad Speaker over OTO Biscuit when the cue should read as a radio, cassette deck, or speaker-in-room rather than abstract bit reduction. Choose Dirty Tape for time-varying wear and dropouts; choose Bad Speaker for repeatable device response, breakup, width, and dry/wet placement.

advanced_moves.setup: On a mono source, audition all three Speaker modes at low Drive, Width fully mono, and Mix fully wet before adding stereo processing.
advanced_moves.action: Choose the physical response first, then increase Width until the treated component separates from the dry center. Blend Mix last and verify mono.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The effect should widen around a stable core; reject settings where mono loses the intended device tone or the source's location becomes ambiguous.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Speaker selection, nonlinear Drive, Width, and parallel Mix are independent decisions; widening before choosing the model can disguise the actual response.

advanced_moves.setup: For dialogue, vocal, or drum perspective, place Bad Speaker on a parallel bus and begin with Cassette Deck or Hi-Fi rather than the most restricted Portable Radio.
advanced_moves.action: Use Tone to fit the return behind the clean source, drive until the speaker character becomes identifiable, then automate the return send rather than changing Drive every section.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The clean source should remain intelligible while the return adds location and grit; avoid comb-like hollowness at intermediate Mix values.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The dedicated dry/wet and modeled speaker responses let device perspective be layered without forcing the direct signal through the same bandwidth restriction.

use_cases.context: Boom bap — Snare and percussion parallel
use_cases.application: Use Cassette Deck for mid bite, add moderate Drive, and narrow Width until the dirty layer reinforces rather than smears the center.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its measured device response supplies resonant speaker breakup that an EQ plus Saturation Knob would not recreate as one behavior.

use_cases.application: Use Hi-Fi Speaker for a room perspective, automate Width and send level, and reserve Portable Radio for brief contrast events.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Three repeatable physical perspectives make spatial storytelling easier than Dirty Tape's random transport damage.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Bad Speaker can occupy either Shape or Drive in Console 1 and can be placed freely in Amp Room Studio mode, enabling placement before or after other nonlinear modules as a meaningful tone change.
avoid_when: Avoid it when exact bit depth, sample clock, or moving tape defects define the effect; use OTO Biscuit or Dirty Tape respectively.

name: Empirical Labs Professor Punch-Knuckles
comparative_edge: Choose Professor over Mike-E Comp when you want its three ELI nonlinearities without configuring a full preamp/compressor. Choose Mike-E for controllable attack, ratio, external sidechain, and separate preamp staging; choose Harmonics when transient reconstruction and non-ELI distortion families are more important than Toasty, Crunchy, or Distress.

advanced_moves.setup: At moderate gain-compensated Drive, compare Toasty, Crunchy, and Distress with post Low Cut, Tone, and High Cut neutral.
advanced_moves.action: Select the transfer behavior first, then compare XFRM, Wide, and Tape at that same moderate amount. Add post filters only after both stages are chosen.
advanced_moves.listen_for: You should hear mode-specific spectral emphasis before heavy distortion makes them converge; reject a choice that is only louder or darker after filtering.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Distortion selects the nonlinear circuit, while Mode changes its tonal emphasis; Mode differences are documented as clearer at moderate drive.

advanced_moves.setup: On a parallel drum or vocal bus, select Distress, Mix fully wet, and begin below 3 dB of gain reduction.
advanced_moves.action: Increase Drive into roughly 3–5 dB of reduction, then lower Mix to restore dry attacks. Use the post filters to keep the crushed layer out of vulnerable extremes.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The source should sit forward with controlled peaks while dry transients remain legible; stop before room noise or breath becomes a continuous floor.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Distress is the Distressor/Mike-E compressor circuit at its fastest aggressive setting, while Mix blends the pre-effect dry signal back in.

use_cases.application: Use Distress for several dB of fast reduction, blend back dry transients, and high-pass the crushed layer after distortion.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It reaches the ELI compression-distortion behavior faster than building the equivalent Mike-E chain.

use_cases.application: Compare Crunchy and Toasty at moderate THD, select Tape emphasis if top-edge breakup should lead, then automate Mix between phrases.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Three ELI circuit types plus separate emphasis and post filtering make vocal aggression repeatable without a full multistage processor.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the meter changes meaning by distortion type—THD percentage for Toasty and Crunchy, gain reduction for Distress. A visually identical reading is not the same measurement across modes.
avoid_when: Avoid it when compressor timing, external sidechain, or a clean preamp state must be controlled explicitly; Mike-E Comp is the fuller ELI tool.

sources.title: Softube Empirical Labs Prof Punch-Knuckles user manual

name: Weiss Exciter
comparative_edge: Choose Weiss Exciter over Harmonics when you want additive harmonics targeted by independent input/output bands, adaptive level behavior, M/S width, and minimal fundamental-EQ shift. Choose Harmonics for full-waveform analog-family distortion and dynamics reconstruction; choose Weiss EQ MP when a static high-frequency lift is sufficient and no new overtones are needed.

advanced_moves.setup: Enable Adaptive and Mastering, choose a harmonic Mode, and define a narrow Pre target band around the fundamentals you want to excite.
advanced_moves.action: Place the Post band at least an octave above the Pre high-pass region, raise Harmonics while monitoring the wet/difference signal, then widen Post only if useful overtones are being excluded.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The added signal should sound related to the source rather than like filtered hiss; bypass should remove vibrancy without collapsing the original tonal balance.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Generated harmonics occur above their fundamentals, and independent pre/post filters separate what creates harmonics from which harmonics reach the output.

advanced_moves.setup: On a stereo master or ambience bus, establish a linked stereo setting, then switch to M/S with Width neutral and channels ganged.
advanced_moves.action: Reduce wet Width or process Side more conservatively if excitation exaggerates ambience; compare minimum-phase and linear-phase only after the harmonic balance is stable.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Crispness should rise without cymbals pulling outward or the phantom center narrowing; check mono for unchanged dry integrity.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Width changes only the wet contribution. Minimum-phase mode phase-compensates the dry path for coherent summing; linear-phase mode leaves that dry path unprocessed.

use_cases.application: Use Adaptive Mastering mode, target fundamentals below the desired sparkle, and monitor only the generated band before blending subtly.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It can add level-stable overtones with reduced fundamental leakage instead of relying on a broad EQ shelf or full-waveform saturation.

use_cases.context: Ambient techno — Reverb and texture bus
use_cases.application: Generate harmonics from a bounded midrange Pre band, constrain their Post band, and reduce wet Side width if the return becomes diffuse.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Independent target/output bands and wet-width control provide more spatial discipline than Harmonics' full-signal drive.

pairings.goal: Set transparent static balance first, then add bounded harmonics instead of another high shelf.
pairings.order: Weiss EQ MP → Weiss Exciter
pairings.setup: Complete cuts and broad balance in EQ MP, match output, then select Exciter Pre fundamentals and Post harmonic range while monitoring the wet contribution.
pairings.why_it_works: EQ MP changes existing spectrum; Exciter adds new overtones on a parallel path and can reduce fundamental leakage in Mastering mode.
pairings.caution: Do not duplicate brightness with an EQ shelf and excitation. Match loudness and check fatigue at low monitor level.

insider_note: Documented behavior: in minimum-phase mode the internal dry/wet paths are phase-compensated to prevent cancellation without linear-phase latency. Linear phase is optional, not required for coherent parallel blending.
avoid_when: Avoid it when obvious clipping, low-frequency thickening, or transient rounding is the goal; Harmonics, Overstayer M-A-S, or Tape is the more direct Softube choice.

name: Dimensions
comparative_edge: Choose it over Core Dimensions when six selector algorithms spanning spring, plate, room/concert hall, random hall, cathedral, and chamber need their own controls; choose it over TSAR-1 when distinct reverb designs matter more than shaping one modern algorithm.

advanced_moves.setup: Vocal send.
advanced_moves.action: Choose plate/chamber, set pre-delay for diction, then shorten high-frequency decay before extending global time.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Long depth that clears the next phrase.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Frequency multipliers decouple spectral decay from nominal time.

advanced_moves.setup: Printed synth/percussion return.
advanced_moves.action: Use Room/Concert Hall or Random Hall, audition System Noise, then print restrained modulation changes and edit the best passages.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A deliberate hardware-era scene change, not zipper noise.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Those algorithms model bandwidth, internal quantization noise, and characteristic modulation rather than adding generic degradation afterward.

use_cases.context: Hybrid orchestral: Brass and strings sends
use_cases.application: Use dense chamber for brass and modulated hall for strings with matched pre-delay logic.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: One plug-in supplies genuinely different spatial lineages.

use_cases.application: Print a noisy early-digital tail and gate it to the bar.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It retains deeper decay shaping than Wasted Space.

insider_note: Documented: several modes model quantization and System Noise rather than adding generic post-processing.
avoid_when: Use Core Dimensions for five streamlined choices or TSAR-1R when fast, consistent controls matter more than historical specificity.

name: Core Dimensions
comparative_edge: Choose it over full Dimensions when five curated algorithms and one consistent control set are faster than algorithm-specific editing. Choose it over TSAR-1 when switching among spring, plate, synth hall, and chamber matters more than independent early-reflection, density, and diffusion controls.

advanced_moves.setup: Lead synth send with kick sidechain.
advanced_moves.action: Select Synth Hall, high-pass it, key external Ducking from kick, then try negative-octave shimmer before octave-up.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A low bloom opening between kicks.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Shimmer precedes the reverb; ducking controls the resulting wet tail.

advanced_moves.setup: Short drum-room aux.
advanced_moves.action: Use Chamber, shorten Time until echoes disappear, then raise Width only while mono-checking.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Body without a weakened snare center.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Chamber stays dense and pitch-stable; Width alters wet mid/side balance afterward.

use_cases.application: Duck a long Synth Hall and automate shimmer only in breakdowns.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Reverb, shimmer, and ducking share one path.

use_cases.application: Use short Chamber with restrained high cut and width.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It stays dense at short decay.

insider_note: Documented: do not automate Algorithm; it can cause noise and CPU spikes.
avoid_when: Use TSAR-1 when early reflections, density, and modulation must be independently controlled.

name: TSAR-1 Reverb
comparative_edge: Choose it over Dimensions when one coherent algorithm must span sparse room to smooth hall. Its separate early-reflection type/mix, density, diffusion, and modulation solve depth and mix-occupancy problems that TSAR-1R hides.

advanced_moves.setup: Long vocal hall.
advanced_moves.action: Set ER Type/Mix first, lower Density until lyric gaps return, then extend Reverb Time and add pre-delay.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Large depth without continuous fog.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Density controls reflection packing independently of RT60.

advanced_moves.setup: Near/far orchestral buses.
advanced_moves.action: Duplicate one setting; on the far bus shorten pre-delay, raise ER Mix, and darken Tone.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Two planes that still sound like one venue.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Early-reflection timing and balance are primary distance cues.

use_cases.application: Stage families with matched tails but different ER balance.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It exposes distance cues hidden by macro reverbs.

use_cases.application: Use long time at low density and automate Tone.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Sparse tails leave rhythmic negative space.

insider_note: Engineering inference: lower Density before shortening a musically correct decay when the tail merely occupies too much energy.
avoid_when: Use TSAR-1R for speed; choose Dimensions for an explicit spring, plate, or early-digital identity.

name: TSAR-1R Reverb
comparative_edge: Choose it over TSAR-1 when a calibrated room-to-hall macro is more useful than independent density, diffusion, and ER controls. Reverb Time coordinates several internal variables, producing fast plausible spaces rather than only lengthening a tail.

advanced_moves.setup: Several instruments needing individual depth.
advanced_moves.action: Set Color by role, sweep Reverb Time until each source moves behind the dry plane, then reduce Mix.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Depth without one obvious shared preset.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Time co-adjusts pre-delay, ER, diffusion, density, and decay.

advanced_moves.setup: Parallel guitar/percussion ambience.
advanced_moves.action: Print a short dark space fully wet, compress the print, and blend beneath dry.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Sustain rises while transients stay intact.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Parallel compression exaggerates the calibrated room envelope.

use_cases.application: Give rhythm guitars slightly different short spaces.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The macro is fast across many tracks.

use_cases.application: Use dark short instances as distance controls.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Less stylized than Dimensions, simpler than TSAR-1.

insider_note: Documented: Reverb Time changes internal pre-delay, ER, diffusion, density, and decay together.
avoid_when: Use TSAR-1 when one room character must remain fixed while density or decay changes independently.

name: Atlantis Dual Chambers
comparative_edge: Choose it over TSAR or Dimensions when two real Atlantis Studios chambers, their speakers, microphones, and capture chain should define the record. It offers physically related spaces to blend, not a synthetic engine pretending to become every room.

advanced_moves.setup: Lead-vocal send.
advanced_moves.action: Solo and tune chamber A, repeat for B, then blend asymmetrically before return EQ.
advanced_moves.listen_for: One chamber locates the singer while the other adds sustain.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Different physical/capture signatures add complementary density.

advanced_moves.setup: Drum-room replacement.
advanced_moves.action: Send snare/toms, compress only the wet bus, and automate the second chamber into fills.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Fills expand while kick and center remain anchored.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Selective sends avoid low buildup; compression extends captured envelopes.

use_cases.application: Level-match and audition both chambers on the lead, then add the contrasting chamber mainly to stacks and endings.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The chambers create a cohesive studio signature.

use_cases.application: Build one shared short chamber and compress gently.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Physical reflections glue live sources credibly.

insider_note: Documented: yellow markings identify Atlantis Studios' normal/original settings, while Mic Distance changes the capture relationship without changing predelay.
avoid_when: Use Core Dimensions for ducking/shimmer or TSAR-1 for continuously variable room architecture.

sources.title: Softube Atlantis Dual Chambers user manual

name: Model 77 Reverb
comparative_edge: Choose it over Core Dimensions Synth Hall when Model 77’s compact vintage-digital space should remain the fingerprint. Its host-module form separates decay and mix but stays a character insert, not a TSAR-1 replacement.

advanced_moves.setup: Model 77 layered patch.
advanced_moves.action: Raise its one-knob reverb until notes join, then shorten layer release so reverb owns overlap.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Lush changes without double-smearing.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The macro links wet level and decay; source release remains independent.

advanced_moves.setup: External send in Modular/Amp Room.
advanced_moves.action: Use fully wet, automate Decay while send level stays fixed, and filter afterward.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Longer scenes without a wet-level jump.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The separated module exposes decay independently.

use_cases.application: Keep shared effects in the Model 77 vocabulary.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its compact vintage space sits inside bright polysynth arrangements.

use_cases.context: Post-rock: Clean guitar in Amp Room
use_cases.application: Put it before light drive on a parallel path.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The dense algorithm becomes amp texture.

insider_note: Documented: the instrument slider links dry/wet and decay; the Modular component separates them.
avoid_when: Use TSAR-1 for acoustic staging or Core Dimensions for shimmer, ducking, and filters.

name: Spring Reverb
comparative_edge: Choose it over Dimensions/Core Dimensions springs when tank mechanics must be playable: spring count, tension, and Shake materially alter response. Choose it over Tape Echoes when spring is needed without heads, tape Dirt, or a feedback loop.

advanced_moves.setup: Filtered dub send.
advanced_moves.action: Use fewer springs, tune Tension, automate Shake only at transitions, and print.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A dramatic strike without uncontrolled low thunder.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Shake excites the physical model; Springs/Tension change density and resonance.

advanced_moves.setup: Parallel pre/post-amp guitar paths.
advanced_moves.action: Match spring settings, then compare pre-amp saturation against post-amp clarity.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Integrated smear balanced by readable pick attack.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: A downstream nonlinearity reshapes the tank tail.

use_cases.application: Use one or two filtered springs and occasional Shake.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Mechanics are performable unlike fixed spring algorithms.

use_cases.application: Use a tighter multi-spring response after a clean amp.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Springs/Tension tune the tank identity directly.

pairings.goal: Build a warm dub throw with mechanically distinct tail and repeat stages.
pairings.order: Tube Delay → Spring Reverb
pairings.setup: Filter a low-feedback Tube Delay return, then send only selected repeats to a one- or two-spring setting.
pairings.why_it_works: Tube saturation rounds the discrete echoes before the spring adds resonant splash and density.
pairings.caution: High delay feedback plus Shake can run away quickly; print the performance and leave headroom.

insider_note: Documented: Springs and Tension are software controls not normally found on tanks; Modular adds CV for them and Shake.
avoid_when: Use TSAR-1, Atlantis, or Dimensions for smooth, believable spaces rather than exposed spring mechanics.

name: Doom Chvrch
comparative_edge: Choose it over TSAR/Dimensions when a stylized Amp Room reverb that can move from boxy room to nearly infinite evolving tail matters more than room realism. Choose Wasted Space for explicit sample-rate and anti-alias-filter degradation, or Spring Reverb for playable tank mechanics.

advanced_moves.setup: Parallel guitar path in Amp Room.
advanced_moves.action: Place it before a driven amp on a parallel path, keep dry guitar separate, shape Bass/Treble before extending Time.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A distorted cloud behind stable attack/pitch.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Pre-amp placement saturates the tail as a continuous source.

advanced_moves.setup: 100% wet transition aux.
advanced_moves.action: Print one phrase tail, gate/reverse the print, and cut it before the next downbeat.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A designed transition with a defined end.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Its deliberately non-realistic, evolving tail can be committed and rearranged as source material.

use_cases.application: Drive the wet path through the amp only at cadences.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its long evolving tail can become part of the high-gain texture.

use_cases.application: Render tails from short metal hits and layer the prints.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The deliberately non-realistic tail is suitable for committed resampling.

insider_note: Engineering inference: pre/post-amp placement is its expert control because the amp either joins the tail generator or stays upstream.
avoid_when: Use Atlantis/TSAR for credible staging; choose Wasted Space for overt digital degradation.

name: Wasted Space
comparative_edge: Choose it over Dimensions when an early-digital plate plus adjustable 2.4–24 kHz sample rate and selectable anti-alias filters must create the artifact. Choose Doom Chvrch for a smoother evolving wash rather than explicit converter behavior.

advanced_moves.setup: Short snare/clap aux.
advanced_moves.action: Set a short Time, lower Sample Rate until grain appears, compare 48/24/12 dB filters, then raise High Pass before any post-gate.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A crunchy halo whose aliasing does not mask the snare attack.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Sample Rate sets the available bandwidth; shallower or disabled anti-alias filtering lets more atonal foldback through.

advanced_moves.setup: Clean synth printed fully wet.
advanced_moves.action: Render the same phrase at several Sample Rate and Filter Type combinations, then resequence only the contrasting tails.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Related tails with clearly different bandwidth and foldback.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The converter model changes the reverb spectrum while the source patch and decay setting remain fixed.

use_cases.application: Use a short decay, reduced Sample Rate, and High Pass before a post-reverb gate.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its converter controls expose the cheap-digital plate identity directly.

use_cases.application: Print syllable tails through contrasting Filter Type and Sample Rate settings, then slice them.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The plate and converter artifacts become repeatable resampling material.

insider_note: Documented: with the 48 dB filter, Sample Rate behaves much like a low-pass limit; with the filter off or shallow, content above half the selected rate folds into atonal aliasing.
avoid_when: Use TSAR-1 or Atlantis for transparent acoustic depth; use Dimensions for degraded color with deeper decay control.

name: Stereo Delay
comparative_edge: Choose it over Echoes when two clear left/right times and fixed 1980s chorus are enough; choose it over Tape Echoes for clean predictable timing. Shared feedback duration keeps unequal channels coherent.

advanced_moves.setup: Mono guitar/synth aux, Ping Pong off.
advanced_moves.action: Set related unequal note values, lower Feedback below phrase overlap, then add Chorus I and darken Tone.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Rhythmic width with a centered source.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Independent times create stereo patterning while feedback length stays shared.

advanced_moves.setup: Vocal word throw.
advanced_moves.action: Use Ping Pong, one synced division, Tone above center, and automate send rather than time.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Alternating echoes that leave center clear.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Ping Pong matches timing; upper Tone positions remove bass.

use_cases.application: Use quarter/eighth asymmetry with Chorus I.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Faster and sparser than Echoes.

use_cases.application: Use bass-reduced synced Ping Pong only on endings.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Cleaner than Tape Echoes but more voiced than stock delay.

pairings.goal: Convert a clean stereo echo pattern into a ducked background space.
pairings.order: Stereo Delay → Core Dimensions
pairings.setup: Set short related left/right times and low feedback, then feed Core Dimensions with external ducking keyed from the dry source.
pairings.why_it_works: The first stage creates width and rhythm; the second smooths repeats and automatically vacates the foreground.
pairings.caution: Mono-check unequal delays and wet width before committing the chain.

insider_note: Documented: Tone below center rolls off treble; above center rolls off bass—it is not a simple tilt.
avoid_when: Use Echoes for composed multi-taps; use Tape Echoes for speed warps, heads, and unstable feedback.

name: Echoes
comparative_edge: Choose it over Stereo Delay for composed tap placement and over Tape Echoes when one patch needs Filter, Reverb, BBD, Tape, Pan, or Lo-fi loop behavior. Up to ten taps make the repeat pattern an arrangement layer.

advanced_moves.setup: Sparse vocal/percussion aux.
advanced_moves.action: Mute all taps, add one center anchor and two quieter off-grid side taps, then choose Pan mode.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A memorable answering rhythm with holes.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Per-tap time/pan/level precede global feedback.

advanced_moves.setup: Chord in BBD mode.
advanced_moves.action: Lengthen time until clock artifacts appear, low-pass them, then print a master-time ride.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Pitch/clock motion behind the chord, not brittle domination.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: BBD time changes modeled clock rate and playback pitch.

use_cases.application: Program three to five shuffled taps around snare gaps.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Two-line delays cannot compose the same syncopation.

use_cases.application: Move sparse taps from Reverb into Lo-fi behavior while printing.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It crosses discrete echo into texture in one pattern.

pairings.goal: Place designed taps behind a source without losing their internal rhythm.
pairings.order: Echoes → TSAR-1 Reverb
pairings.setup: Create a sparse tap pattern with little global feedback, then use a short, low-density TSAR-1 tail on the delay return.
pairings.why_it_works: Tap timing remains the compositional layer while TSAR-1 supplies a controllable acoustic envelope.
pairings.caution: Long feedback and high reverb density can collapse the pattern into an undifferentiated wash.

insider_note: Documented: Tape Drive changes feedback markedly; BBD time changes pitch of audio already in the line.
avoid_when: Use Stereo Delay for two-line rhythm, Tube Delay for simple warm slap, or Tape Echoes for hands-on head feedback.

name: Tape Echoes
comparative_edge: Choose it over Echoes when playback heads, tape Drive/Dirt, spring-style reverb, and self-oscillation should behave as one performable machine. Choose it over Tube Delay for speed instability and dropout; Just Dirt also colors without audible repeats.

advanced_moves.setup: Dub aux with loop filters visible.
advanced_moves.action: Start with one head, filter lows, fade toward three heads while riding Feedback, then use Echoes On to stop new input.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A rising cloud that exits cleanly.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Head count changes loop density; Echoes On leaves existing repeats intact.

advanced_moves.setup: Drum/keys insert at Just Dirt.
advanced_moves.action: Level-match Drive, raise Dirt to first rhythmic dropouts, then compare Dual/Normal Stereo in mono.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Tape motion without perceivable echo or unstable center.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Just Dirt forces zero heads while retaining coloration.

use_cases.application: Ride heads and Feedback, then close input before the kick returns.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: More playable than Echoes for feedback gestures.

use_cases.application: Use Just Dirt with no audible heads.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Adds tape wear without a full tape-machine processor.

pairings.goal: Separate tape-repeat motion from a more exposed mechanical splash.
pairings.order: Tape Echoes → Spring Reverb
pairings.setup: Use one or two playback heads with filtered feedback, turn Tape Echoes' own reverb down, and send the return into a restrained spring.
pairings.why_it_works: The tape loop supplies evolving repeats; the dedicated spring exposes controllable spring count, tension, and Shake.
pairings.caution: Do not run two spring stages by accident; verify Tape Echoes' internal reverb is reduced.

insider_note: Documented: placing reverb before echoes makes it recur inside the loop; parallel mode behaves conventionally.
avoid_when: Use Stereo Delay for pristine timing or Echoes for exact per-tap composition.

name: Tube Delay
comparative_edge: Choose it over Tape Echoes when tube compression/grit should replace wow and head patterns. Choose it over Stereo Delay for a mono-focused echo whose nominally dry and wet paths can be driven separately.

advanced_moves.setup: Bass/vocal insert, Mix dry.
advanced_moves.action: Set Direct Drive and level-match, then add short delay and tune Delay Drive; revisit Mix after each drive change.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Source thickens before a denser repeat appears.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Separate tube stages color direct and post-feedback paths.

advanced_moves.setup: Parallel drum thickener.
advanced_moves.action: Use sub-slap time, low Feedback, strong wet drive, and filter cymbals from the return.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A compressed shadow with no countable repeat.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Short separation plus post-delay tube compression reinforces body.

use_cases.application: Lightly drive direct path and add a bass-controlled short repeat.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Integrates preamp color and slap more tightly than Stereo Delay.

use_cases.application: Blend a driven sub-100 ms wet return.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Adds harmonic thickness without tape pitch instability.

pairings.goal: Give a warm vocal throw a physical studio-chamber finish.
pairings.order: Tube Delay → Atlantis Dual Chambers
pairings.setup: Set a short filtered Tube Delay with low feedback, then send the return to one Atlantis chamber and automate the second only at phrase ends.
pairings.why_it_works: Tube Delay rounds the repeat; the captured chambers add a consistent real-space signature.
pairings.caution: Level-match the two chambers and high-pass the chain if repeated consonants or low notes accumulate.

insider_note: Documented: Direct Drive means the dry path is a tube preamp; tone controls also change distortion behavior.
avoid_when: Use Stereo Delay for untouched dry/stereo rhythm or Tape Echoes for multi-head instability.

name: Model 84 Chorus
comparative_edge: Choose it over Fix Doubler for a fixed two-speed synth-chorus circuit, and over Widener when audible modulation is welcome. Mode I/II and mono/stereo reproduce the modeled instrument’s constrained output choices.

advanced_moves.setup: Mono synth/guitar stereo insert.
advanced_moves.action: Choose Mode I, raise input to first thickening, back off, then compare mono/stereo while mono-checking.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Width without hard center loss or crunch.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The modeled stage distorts when driven and stereo exposes dual outputs.

advanced_moves.setup: Parallel keyboard/drum print.
advanced_moves.action: Print Mode II wet, high-pass it, and automate into fills.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Fast animated lift with intact low transient.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Mode II is faster; filtering confines decorrelation.

use_cases.application: Use Mode I stereo in verses and a parallel Mode II lift in choruses.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Immediate 1980s circuit behavior.

use_cases.application: Blend Mode I above the fundamental against mono dry bass.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: More characterful than artifact-minimizing Widener.

insider_note: Documented: Modes I and II cannot combine, and high input can distort the chorus.
avoid_when: Use Fix Doubler for adjustable rate/depth/randomization or Widener for subtler width and mono tools.

name: Fix Flanger and Doubler
comparative_edge: Choose the full pair over Fix Doubler when one session needs both controlled ADT and manual/through-zero tape flanging. It beats Model 84 Chorus for adjustable time motion and Widener for overt effects.

advanced_moves.setup: Printed transition with latency compensation.
advanced_moves.action: Set negative polarity, 50% Mix, Regen off, manually chase VSO through zero, then comp the best sweep.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A deep cancellation crossing smoothly.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Equal inverted dry/delay cancels at zero time.

advanced_moves.setup: Backing-vocal bus.
advanced_moves.action: Use medium Offset, low Random Sweep, Stereo/Dual Sweep, and lower Mix until consonants center.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Extra performers without periodic chorus.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Random pitch and channel delay decorrelate the copy.

use_cases.application: Perform and edit a manual flange into the section change.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: VSO chase exceeds fixed modulation tools.

use_cases.application: Use randomized stereo doubling at low depth.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: One package handles natural ADT and special flanging.

pairings.goal: Add a stable short room after animated doubling.
pairings.order: Fix Flanger and Doubler → TSAR-1R Reverb
pairings.setup: Keep modulation depth modest and feedback controlled, then use a dark short TSAR-1R setting after it.
pairings.why_it_works: Modulation supplies motion and apparent width; the calibrated macro reverb keeps that motion in a bounded space.
pairings.caution: Too much modulation before a long reverb multiplies pitch smear and weakens localization.

insider_note: Documented: true through-zero needs 50% Mix, negative polarity, Regen off; the flanger adds compensatable latency.
avoid_when: Avoid live use if latency is unacceptable; use Fix Doubler alone for routine ADT or Fix Phaser for all-pass motion.

sources.title: Softube Fix Flanger and Doubler manual

name: Fix Doubler
comparative_edge: Choose it over Layers when one controlled duplicate is more credible than a multi-layer effect; choose it over Model 84 Chorus when offset, waveform, randomization, and stereo behavior must follow the performer.

advanced_moves.setup: Stereo lead-vocal insert.
advanced_moves.action: Set Offset by syllable speed, low Random Sweep/Rate, enable Stereo, and raise Mix only until vowels widen.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Spread vowels with centered consonants.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Random motion avoids cyclic chorus; offset separates without a second word.

advanced_moves.setup: Wet-only guitar print.
advanced_moves.action: Use short Offset, Sine Sweep, no dry, print and pan opposite the original.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A separately editable pseudo-take that still survives a mono check.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Wet isolation allows independent timing, panning, and downstream processing; it does not remove comb filtering when recombined.

use_cases.application: Automate subtle Random Auto Double higher only in chorus.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: More controlled and less dense than Layers.

use_cases.application: Print and route the duplicate into a second amp color.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Creates an editable copy unlike Widener.

insider_note: Documented: Regen is disabled in Auto Double; Random is most natural at low Sweep/Rate.
avoid_when: Use Layers for a crowd/octaves, Widener for no audible performer, or Model 84 Chorus for fixed vintage motion.

sources.title: Softube Fix Flanger and Doubler manual

name: Fix Phaser
comparative_edge: Choose it over Fix Flanger for a finite set of uneven all-pass notches without literal delay sweep; choose it over Widener when phase coloration is musical. Stages, bipolar envelope, stereo modes, and sync make it both articulator and modulation effect.

advanced_moves.setup: Rhythmic guitar/clavinet.
advanced_moves.action: Use Fast envelope, low LFO Sweep, bipolar Envelope, four stages, then add Regen.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Each pick drives vowel motion without constant swoosh.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Amplitude moves modal centers; stages/feedback set notch density.

advanced_moves.setup: Static pad needing width.
advanced_moves.action: Select Wide, many stages, Sweep minimum, tune Offset/Regen while mono-checking.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Side motion with stable center.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Wide retains preset movement independent of Sweep.

use_cases.application: Let accents drive four-stage notch motion.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: More articulation-sensitive than fixed chorus.

use_cases.application: Use ten stages, synced sweep, and automate Regen.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: All-pass motion is more audible than Widener by design.

pairings.goal: Turn a moving notch pattern into an evolving dark texture.
pairings.order: Fix Phaser → Doom Chvrch
pairings.setup: Automate a slow shallow phaser on a parallel source, then feed that path into a dark long Doom Chvrch tail.
pairings.why_it_works: The phaser continuously changes which frequencies excite the reverb, creating motion without modulating the reverb itself.
pairings.caution: High resonance can make a narrow frequency dominate the entire tail.

insider_note: Documented: 50% Mix gives deepest cancellation; Wide still moves with Sweep at zero.
avoid_when: Use Fix Doubler for natural ADT, Widener for subtler width, or Fix Flanger for through-zero comb cancellation.

name: Layers
comparative_edge: Choose it over Fix Doubler for several apparent performances plus an independent widening stage; choose it over Widener when pitch/time drift and octave relationships must create density before spatial processing.

advanced_moves.setup: Lead-vocal chorus bus, dry outside.
advanced_moves.action: Create two differently drifting layers, filter wet lows, widen Wet Only, and automate layer level.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Chorus-sized image with centered consonants/low end.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Drift decorrelates layers while Wet Only spares dry.

advanced_moves.setup: Mono synth line.
advanced_moves.action: Build near-unison and quieter octave layers, use Slow Mod, then set Mono Bass.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Harmonic enlargement without a separate octave voice.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Pitch layering and side filtering are independent.

use_cases.application: Add low-level drifting layers and widen only them.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Builds mass beyond Fix Doubler.

use_cases.application: Band-limit octave layers with Slow Mod.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Separately exaggerates pitch, time, and width.

insider_note: Documented: it inherits five Widener algorithms, adds Slow Mod, and can filter/widen wet layers only.
avoid_when: Use Fix Doubler for one subtle copy or Widener when no extra voices should exist.

name: Widener
comparative_edge: Choose it over Layers when no extra performers are needed, and over Model 84 Chorus when width should minimize periodic motion. Its five methods place artifacts differently, while correlation/goniometer tools make it the deliberate bus choice.

advanced_moves.setup: Mono percussion bus.
advanced_moves.action: Compare Frequency Spread and Rotation level-matched; move low boundary or Emphasis until panning stops, then reduce Amount.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Width without shifted center or softened punch.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The algorithms relocate phase artifacts differently.

advanced_moves.setup: Stereo stem with meters visible.
advanced_moves.action: Use low Reflections Amount, darken added field, keep Width 100%, set Mono Bass, and mono-check.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A larger space with no audible slap/collapse.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Modulated short echoes mask combing; Mono Bass removes low sides.

use_cases.application: Apply Frequency Spread above low mids.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Band-bounded phase width is subtler than chorus.

use_cases.application: Use dark low-level Reflections.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Adds short-space width without a long tail or fake take.

insider_note: Documented: leave output Width near 100% and use algorithm Amount; Rotation does little for already-stereo input.
avoid_when: Use Layers/Fix Doubler for audible copies or Model 84 Chorus for overt modulation.

name: Lion Head Vibrato
comparative_edge: Choose it over Tinnerö for pitch rather than amplitude motion, and over Model 84 Chorus when the source should visibly bend rather than split into an ensemble. Random/Multisine and Vibe/Stereo make chain placement decisive.

advanced_moves.setup: Clean guitar post-amp.
advanced_moves.action: Use Random, low Depth/Speed, Stereo, then raise Depth while checking double-stops and mono.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Non-cyclical dimension without unstable chord tuning.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Random avoids repeated LFO signature.

advanced_moves.setup: Parallel path before driven amp.
advanced_moves.action: Use Vibe/Multisine at moderate depth, distort separately, blend under dry.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Fused wobble with stable pitch anchor.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Pre-amp pitch motion changes what enters nonlinearity.

use_cases.application: Use post-amp Random stereo movement.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Less fixed than Model 84 Chorus.

use_cases.application: Drive a deep wet path into distortion/reverb beside dry fundamental.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: True pitch motion creates beating Tinnerö cannot.

pairings.goal: Spread subtle tape-like pitch movement through a sustained wash.
pairings.order: Lion Head Vibrato → Doom Chvrch
pairings.setup: Place shallow vibrato before a dark parallel reverb and keep an unprocessed dry anchor.
pairings.why_it_works: The long tail integrates small pitch offsets into width and motion.
pairings.caution: Keep pitch depth restrained on bass or harmonically dense material.

insider_note: Engineering inference: post-amp preserves drive consistency; pre-amp fuses vibrato into distortion but reduces stability.
avoid_when: Use Tinnerö for rhythmic level pulses or Widener when perceptual pitch must remain fixed.

name: Tinnerö Tremolo
comparative_edge: Choose it over Lion Head when level—not pitch—must articulate rhythm, and over Fix Phaser when moving notches are unnecessary. Dynamics can preserve attack and reveal tremolo mainly in sustained tails.

advanced_moves.setup: Sustained guitar/e-piano.
advanced_moves.action: Set audible Speed/Depth, raise Dynamics until attacks stay present, then reduce Depth after level matching.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Clear onset followed by blooming tremolo.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Dynamics retains more direct behavior around stronger input.

advanced_moves.setup: Very slow parallel pad tremolo.
advanced_moves.action: Keep dry anchor and automate wet return so quiet-phase arrivals become arrangement holes.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Intentional long-form breathing.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Slow cycles can begin on a quiet phase.

use_cases.application: Use low-Dynamics tremolo while preserving pick attack.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: No pitch wobble or phase coloration.

use_cases.application: Raise Dynamics, then feed the moving sustain into a clean hall.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Source-responsive tremolo is more organic than fixed LFO depth.

pairings.goal: Create repeats whose amplitude pattern evolves before entering the feedback machine.
pairings.order: Tinnerö Tremolo → Tape Echoes
pairings.setup: Tune Speed by ear to a useful relationship with the song, then feed one playback head at moderate feedback.
