advanced_moves.listen_for: A vocal-like guitar midrange that remains audible without simply becoming louder.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Separating pedal clipping from amp clipping keeps the classic mid contour recognizable.

insider_note: The low-Drive/high-Level metal recipe is not magic gain stacking: it is pre-distortion equalization. The pedal's documented mid boost means the amp clips a more focused spectrum, which is why reducing amp Gain afterward often sounds heavier.
avoid_when: Avoid it when the source already has narrow, nasal mids or needs full-bodied distortion; the RAT-style Kraft is broader. For transparent loudness into an amp, use a clean boost rather than asking TUBE's voicing to disappear.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Marshall Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Progressive metal, use low Drive/high Level into ENGL, then lower the amp's own gain after the pedal is engaged.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its predictable pre-emphasis tightens the detector input more surgically than Kraft's fuller RAT-style clipping.

use_cases.application: In Blues rock, use higher pedal Drive into a mostly clean Pacific Black and roll guitar volume back for verses.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The fixed mid focus keeps the lead forward while the clean amp preserves dynamic cleanup.

pairings.goal: Turn loose high-gain low end into faster palm-muted response.
pairings.order: TUBE Overdrive → American Mainstayer
pairings.setup: Use near-minimum Drive and elevated Level, set Tone by pick clarity, then lower Mainstayer Gain rather than stacking equal amounts of both distortions.
pairings.why_it_works: The pedal’s documented mid emphasis reshapes which bands dominate the amp’s nonlinear stages.
pairings.caution: This is pre-distortion EQ as much as overdrive; it is the wrong move when the amp already sounds thin or the part needs loose scale.

name: Kraft
comparative_edge: Choose Kraft as Softube's unlicensed RAT-family counterpoint to TUBE: fuller low mids, harder clipping, and a wider path from warm drive into fuzzy sustain. TUBE remains the faster choice for the familiar Tube Screamer low-cut/mid-push tightening move.

advanced_moves.setup: Put Kraft on a parallel send from bass or synth bass.
advanced_moves.action: Drive the send harder than you would an insert, turn Filter clockwise to darken the RAT-style edge, high-pass the return, and blend below the clean source.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The line remains deep in the center but reads clearly on small speakers and through dense guitars.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Kraft retains more body across its gain range, while the filtered parallel return isolates its harmonics from the clean fundamental.

advanced_moves.setup: Use Kraft before a clean amp and automate only its Volume between verse and chorus.
advanced_moves.action: Set Distortion for the chorus texture, lower Volume until the verse is nearly clean, then raise Volume so both pedal and amp contribute in the chorus.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The chorus expands in density without changing to an unrelated distortion timbre.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Output automation changes both pedal audibility and the following amp's operating point while preserving the pedal's tone setting.

insider_note: Softube does not name the donor, but Kraft's black wedge enclosure and exact Distortion/Filter/Volume control vocabulary identify the Pro Co RAT/RAT 2 family. On bass, a band-limited parallel lane keeps that full-bodied clipping from crowding the fundamental.
avoid_when: Avoid it when you need a repeatable Tube-Screamer-style tightening curve; use TUBE Overdrive. For speaker or tape degradation rather than pedal clipping, Bad Speaker or Dirty Tape creates a more source-specific texture.

use_cases.application: In Synthwave, blend a high-passed Kraft return for growl while keeping the oscillator fundamental dry and centered.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Kraft's full-bodied RAT-style clipping and broad gain range suit synth harmonics better than TUBE's fixed guitar-oriented mid focus.

use_cases.application: In Indie pop, automate output into the same amp across sections, using one tone-filter position for continuity.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The RAT-family gain range covers both warm edge and fuzzy chorus sustain without changing pedals or amp.

pairings.goal: Add audible bass harmonics while the suite DI retains a stable fundamental.
pairings.order: Split in Amp Room Bass Suite: clean DI parallel to Kraft → amp/cab mid lane
pairings.setup: Set the DI bandwidth first, drive Kraft on the high-passed parallel lane, and blend the lane from silence until the bass reads on small speakers.
pairings.why_it_works: Kraft supplies full-bodied RAT-style distortion while the separate DI prevents its low-frequency drive from replacing the clean foundation.
pairings.caution: Phase-align the lanes before bus compression and avoid letting both paths own the same sub range.

name: Lion Head Vibrato (Amp Room)
comparative_edge: Choose Lion Head over Tinnerö when actual pitch motion, not volume pulsing, should make the part feel unstable. Choose Model 84 Chorus or Fix Doubler when ensemble width is more important than a single, audible pitch trajectory.

advanced_moves.setup: Place Lion Head after a mostly clean amp and choose Random waveform.
advanced_moves.action: Keep Speed and Depth low, engage stereo only after the mono motion feels natural, and level-match because widened modulation can appear louder.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Sustains feel alive without each note advertising an obvious periodic wobble.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Random modulation avoids a fixed cycle, while post-amp placement moves the complete recorded tone.

advanced_moves.setup: Place Lion Head after a dirty amp for an obvious effect transition.
advanced_moves.action: Use Vibe mode with Multisine, automate Depth into phrase endings, and narrow or mono the low-frequency lane before the effect.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Leads bend into a controlled seasick tail while their attacks remain centered.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Multiple modulation components create complex pitch motion; band-limiting keeps low-frequency stereo pitch shifts from pulling the image.

insider_note: Softube's own manual suggests Random after a cleanish amp for subtle dimension and Vibe/Multisine after a dirty amp for stronger vintage motion. The useful secret is placement: the same settings feel far more integrated before versus after distortion.
avoid_when: Avoid it on sources where stable pitch and mono center are non-negotiable; use Tinnerö for rhythmic movement or Layers/Fix Doubler for controlled width. Deep stereo settings should be mono-checked before committing.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Vintage Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Psychedelic soul, use slow Random motion after the amp and before a short chamber, with shallow stereo depth.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Lion Head adds aged pitch drift without the obvious ensemble signature of chorus.

use_cases.application: In Desert rock, automate Vibe/Multisine depth on held notes after distortion, leaving fast passages nearly dry.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its pitch trajectory turns sustain into a performance effect where Tinnerö would only pulse loudness.

pairings.goal: Turn irregular pitch drift into an evolving stereo ambience rather than a dry modulation effect.
pairings.order: Lion Head Vibrato → Doom Chvrch
pairings.setup: Use shallow Random movement first, then a dark low-mix Doom Chvrch tail; increase reverb Time before increasing vibrato Depth.
pairings.why_it_works: Pitch variation continuously changes what enters the modulated reverb, creating motion in the decay without destabilizing the dry attack as much.
pairings.caution: Deep stereo vibrato plus long stereo reverb can make the center vanish; check mono and keep lows comparatively dry.

name: Tinnerö Tremolo (Amp Room)
comparative_edge: Choose Tinnerö over amp tremolo when placement and envelope response matter, and over Lion Head when rhythmic amplitude motion is desired without changing pitch. Its Dynamics control can preserve attacks while letting the tremolo emerge on note tails.

advanced_moves.setup: For conventional tremolo, place Tinnerö after drive with Dynamics at zero.
advanced_moves.action: Set Speed in musical relation to the part by ear, raise Depth until the pulse reads, then back it down while listening against kick and hi-hat.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The guitar creates a complementary rhythm rather than fighting the existing percussion grid.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: With Dynamics removed, the full signal follows the modulation waveform predictably.

advanced_moves.setup: For tail-only movement, use sustained chords and raise Dynamics.
advanced_moves.action: Set a faster Speed than the traditional patch, increase Dynamics until attacks pass nearly intact, and place reverb after Tinnerö.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The chord begins solid, then breaks into a pulsing tail that feeds the reverb.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Dynamics restores direct attack and makes modulation become more audible as the played envelope decays.

insider_note: At very slow Speed a new note may land in the waveform's quiet phase and nearly disappear. The documented workaround is not merely less Depth: raise Dynamics to blend back direct signal and make the performance dependable.
avoid_when: Avoid it when the movement must be pitch-based, chorused, or stereo-ensemble-like; use Lion Head, Model 84 Chorus, or Fix Doubler. For strict tempo divisions with numerical sync, verify the current plug-in's control options before relying on a free-running feel.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Vintage Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Americana, use low Depth and modest Dynamics after the amp so attacks stay natural and held notes move gently.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It offers subtler envelope-aware motion than a fixed-depth amp tremolo.

use_cases.application: In Experimental electronic, set extremely slow Speed, automate Dynamics, and print several passes for unpredictable gaps and swells.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its unusually slow range and direct-signal recovery create broken shapes without changing pitch.

pairings.goal: Keep a pulsing source intelligible while a simple room/hall tail fills the amplitude gaps.
pairings.order: Tinnerö Tremolo → TSAR-1R Reverb
pairings.setup: Set Tinnerö Dynamics to preserve attacks, establish Speed/Depth in the groove, then add a short-to-medium TSAR-1R decay after it.
pairings.why_it_works: The tremolo rhythm is imprinted on the reverb input while TSAR-1R supplies space without another complex modulation layer.
pairings.caution: A long, loud tail can average out the pulse; shorten decay or lower wet level before increasing tremolo depth.

name: Doom Chvrch (Amp Room)
comparative_edge: Choose Doom Chvrch over Spring Reverb for a dark, synthetic space that can evolve into an effect, and over TSAR-1 when realism and detailed early/late control are less important than one dramatic Time gesture. It is particularly valuable before distortion, where most reverbs become too polite.

advanced_moves.setup: Place Doom Chvrch before a driven amp with Mix below 20% as a starting point.
advanced_moves.action: Shorten Time until individual chord attacks still register, reduce Bass on the reverb, then raise amp drive just enough to fuse reflections into the sustain.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A continuous wall behind the performance without kick-range wash or lost chord changes.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Pre-amp placement distorts the reverb tail along with the dry signal; filtering prevents low-frequency decay from dominating the nonlinear stage.

advanced_moves.setup: Place it after the amp for phrase-end throws.
advanced_moves.action: Keep Mix low during phrases, automate it upward only on final notes, and lengthen Time after the send rises; return both controls before the next attack.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A tail that blooms after the phrase without smearing the next line.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Separating input amount from decay length creates a throw without leaving a permanently dense reverb bed.

insider_note: The tank comes from the large hall developed for Parallels, while modulation and diffusion draw inspiration from early digital reverb. Softube explicitly says it was not designed to sound realistic—use that as permission to automate it as an instrument.
avoid_when: Avoid it for believable rooms, transparent vocal space, or dense mixes needing predictable decay; TSAR-1/1R or Atlantis is easier to seat. Use Spring Reverb when the source needs a distinct physical splash rather than an evolving synthetic tail.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room ENGL Savage Mark II Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Post-metal, automate post-amp Mix and Time only on final chords, with Bass reduced and the dry riff untouched.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its near-infinite, evolving tail creates an arrangement event rather than a realistic room.

use_cases.application: In Dark ambient, run the reverb before mild amp drive and print a long performance while slowly moving Time and tone.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The algorithm's intentionally artificial modulation survives saturation as a shifting texture better than a natural hall.

pairings.goal: Create a distorted reverb wall whose dry transient still defines the phrase.
pairings.order: Doom Chvrch at low Mix → TUBE Overdrive or driven amp
pairings.setup: Shorten and darken Doom Chvrch first, then raise overdrive only until reflections fuse around the note; automate reverb input on phrase endings.
pairings.why_it_works: Putting reverb before distortion makes the nonlinear stage compress and harmonically bind dry signal and tail into one texture.
pairings.caution: Low-frequency decay can dominate the distortion detector; reduce reverb Bass and keep a separate dry path.

name: Blaze Works Amplification
comparative_edge: Choose Blaze Works over the larger Metal Suite when two focused modern voices are enough: Overvolt II for a simplified 5150-inspired workhorse and Arc Line IV for cleaner-to-high-gain British boutique flexibility. Choose ENGL when licensed multi-channel precision and a broader cabinet set matter.

advanced_moves.setup: Reamp the same DI through Overvolt II and Arc Line IV with the shared German Viper cabinet.
advanced_moves.action: Match distortion density and output, not knob positions. Use Overvolt Gain as the main sweep; on Arc Line select channel first, then set Gain and Depth.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Overvolt emphasizes immediate aggression; Arc Line leaves more channel-dependent clean-to-lead range and adjustable low fullness.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The products use different architectures, while the fixed cabinet makes the amp comparison meaningful.

advanced_moves.setup: Quad-track a tight rhythm part with Overvolt II.
advanced_moves.action: Reduce Gain until a single take sounds slightly under-saturated, vary pick position or cabinet mic across pairs, and high-pass only after all four tracks play.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The combined part sounds saturated but consonants and stops remain synchronized.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Layering multiplies distortion and low-mid energy; lower per-take gain preserves timing cues.

insider_note: The manual names the inspirations directly but the product is a Softube fictional brand. The practical advantage is simplified control: Overvolt deliberately reduces a 5150-style concept to one channel, which makes repeatable multi-track settings faster.
avoid_when: Avoid Blaze Works when you need the original amp's full channel/voicing behavior or licensed reference cabinets; ENGL Savage is deeper. For loose American rectifier mass rather than 5150-inspired focus, use American Mainstayer.

sources.title: Softube Blaze Works Amplification user manual

use_cases.application: In Djent, use lower-gain Overvolt tracks through two mic positions, keeping Depth out of the equation.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its single-channel Gain sweep is fast to standardize across many tightly edited takes.

use_cases.context: Clean verse and saturated chorus guitar
use_cases.source_or_bus: Clean verse and saturated chorus guitar
use_cases.application: In Modern hard rock, use Arc Line's Clean, Normal, and Boost channels rather than switching whole amp rigs between sections.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Channel continuity keeps the underlying voicing stable while the arrangement changes gain role.

pairings.goal: Separate modern high-gain amp choice from speaker breakup, age, and cabinet scale.
pairings.order: Blaze Works amp with cabinet bypassed → Celestion Speaker Shaper
pairings.setup: Choose Overvolt or Arc Line through one neutral Speaker Shaper setup, then alter cabinet back/diameter and speaker distortion after the amp is approved.
pairings.why_it_works: The amp determines distortion envelope while Speaker Shaper changes the physical playback behavior without requiring a new amp performance.
pairings.caution: Avoid heavy speaker distortion on an already saturated amp until the cleanest cabinet configuration is level matched.

name: Amp Room ENGL Savage Mark II Suite
comparative_edge: Choose ENGL over Mainstayer or the generic Metal Suite when extended-range articulation and channel-specific control are central. The 120W/6550 and 60W/EL34 heads are separate voicings, not a size switch; five matched ENGL cabinets make the suite unusually coherent for controlled comparisons.

advanced_moves.setup: Hold channel, gain, cabinet, and mic constant while comparing the 120W and 60W heads.
advanced_moves.action: Level-match, play the same DI, and choose by low-end authority versus midrange compression before adding a boost or post EQ.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The 120W version feels firmer and broader; the 60W EL34 version yields and speaks through the mids sooner.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Different power tubes and power sections change feel and harmonic balance even after output is matched.

advanced_moves.setup: Use the suite's Sleipner boost with amp Gain lower than the target preset.
advanced_moves.action: Choose boost character, raise Amount modestly, and sweep Tightness while palm muting; stop before the lows vanish, then restore only the needed amp gain.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Muted notes end cleanly but open chords retain lower-mid size.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Tightness changes the spectrum entering distortion rather than correcting a flubby result afterward.

insider_note: The suite's low-end compressor is designed specifically to tame or enhance palm-muted chugs. That is more targeted than full-band bus compression: use it to regulate the energy that triggers apparent 'flub' before broad dynamics control.
avoid_when: Avoid ENGL when the song benefits from power-stage looseness, vintage sag, or coarse punk midrange; Mainstayer, Plexi, or JMP 2203 will feel less controlled. The suite is excessive when one fixed amp/cab is all the session needs.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room ENGL Savage Mark II Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Progressive metal, use the 120W head, Lean/Bold mid voicing, and the most articulate matched cabinet before considering an external boost.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The licensed channel and mid circuits preserve interval clarity under gain more predictably than Mainstayer.

use_cases.application: In Melodic death metal, use the 60W head in a smoother mode with less gain and Särimner delay after the amp, keeping rhythm guitars on the 120W voice.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The two power sections create lead/rhythm contrast while remaining inside one matched ENGL cabinet ecosystem.

pairings.goal: Apply the familiar low-cut/mid-push tightening option when the suite’s own Sleipner boost is not the desired character.
pairings.order: TUBE Overdrive → ENGL Savage Mark II
pairings.setup: Start without the pedal, choose head/channel/cab, then add low Drive/high Level and reduce amp Gain until attack returns.
pairings.why_it_works: The pedal changes the spectrum entering the licensed amp model, while the lower amp gain prevents compression from accumulating.
pairings.caution: The suite already includes a purpose-built Tightness control in Sleipner; compare rather than stacking both boosts.

name: Amp Room Marshall Suite
comparative_edge: Choose the suite over individual Marshalls when an arrangement needs era changes inside one cabinet/mic ecosystem: Bluesbreaker softness, Plexi power-stage complexity, JMP/JCM focus, and Jubilee sustain. Choose Metal Suite if licensed Marshall history matters less than broad modern high-gain coverage.

advanced_moves.setup: Record one clean DI and copy a neutral cabinet/mic chain across multistates.
advanced_moves.action: Compare Bluesbreaker, Plexi, JMP, and Jubilee at matched loudness and similar distortion density; only after choosing the envelope, audition the historically matched cabinet.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The amp's attack/recovery suits the performance before cabinet flavor flatters it.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Holding the recording chain constant separates gain architecture from familiar cabinet signatures.

advanced_moves.setup: Build a layered rock arrangement from one Marshall family rather than increasing gain on every track.
advanced_moves.action: Use Bluesbreaker or low-gain Plexi for wide rhythms, JMP for the focused center, and Jubilee for sustained leads; keep room and mic distance consistent across layers.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Each layer has a distinct envelope and midrange role but still sounds recorded in one room.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Different amp generations create separation while shared capture cues provide production cohesion.

insider_note: A useful controlled shootout is to keep the same Amp Room cabinet and mic while swapping amps, then restore matched cabs afterward. This engineering-inference workflow prevents iconic cabinet signatures from deciding the amp comparison for you.
avoid_when: Avoid the full suite when one known Marshall model is enough; the individual plug-in or Amplifiers companion is faster. For rectifier-style lows, ENGL precision, or modern metal boosts, Metal Suite covers more unrelated high-gain territory.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Marshall Suite product page and manual

use_cases.application: In Classic rock, standardize two cabinets and one room, then assign Bluesbreaker, Plexi, and JMP by song density rather than rebuilding rigs per track.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The suite supplies historically related amps inside one recallable platform.

use_cases.application: In Pop punk, use lower-gain JMP/JCM wide and Jubilee for the sustained hook, keeping Guv'nor or TUBE only on the center part.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Marshall midrange stays coherent while gain role changes, avoiding the scooped mismatch of unrelated modern amps.

name: Marshall Bluesbreaker 1962
comparative_edge: Choose Bluesbreaker over Plexi for softer attack, earlier compression, and open-back combo bloom; choose Pacific Black for more scooped clean headroom. It excels when guitar-volume cleanup and player dynamics should remain part of the mix decision.

advanced_moves.setup: Turn the amp up to the target lead breakup and leave the guitar volume below maximum.
advanced_moves.action: Record rhythm with the guitar rolled back, then open it for fills without changing the plug-in; level automation can correct section balance after the performance.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Rhythm cleans without losing harmonic continuity, and fills gain sustain rather than just output.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The whole amp moves through clean and breakup as input falls, preserving a common rectified envelope.

advanced_moves.setup: Blend a dynamic mic for bite with a ribbon or darker mic for body on the combo cabinet.
advanced_moves.action: Solo each, align phase, and bring the body mic up only until thin notes fill out; do not start with equal levels.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Pick definition stays forward while the lower mids bloom after it.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Asymmetric mic roles preserve the combo's transient-to-body movement instead of averaging both perspectives.

insider_note: The modeled reference amp uses a GZ34 tube rectifier. Practical inference: do not immediately 'fix' its yielding attack with fast compression; that envelope is the reason it separates from the firmer Marshall models.
avoid_when: Avoid it for tight palm-muted rhythms, rigid low end, or heavy preamp saturation; JMP 2203, ENGL, or Mainstayer is more direct. Use Pacific when a cleaner, wider pedal platform is the actual requirement.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Marshall Suite user manual

use_cases.context: Single performance covering rhythm and lead
use_cases.source_or_bus: Single performance covering rhythm and lead
use_cases.application: In Blues, set lead breakup at the amp and ride the guitar volume for cleaner verses, using automation only for final level.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its rectifier softness and early compression reward performance control more than JMP's preamp-focused gain.

use_cases.application: In Roots rock, use moderate breakup and a darker body mic so the slide sustains without abrasive upper mids.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Bluesbreaker's softer attack supports vocal slide phrasing better than the firmer Plexi or Custom.

name: Marshall Plexi Super Lead 1959
comparative_edge: Choose Plexi over Bluesbreaker for firmer, louder power-stage authority and over JMP 2203 when non-master-volume complexity matters more than compact preamp focus. Its bright/normal channel blend is the primary tone control before any post EQ.

advanced_moves.setup: Classic four-input Marshall move — jumper the Plexi's bright and normal channels, then start with the bright path carrying the part.
advanced_moves.action: Raise the normal channel only until low strings gain body, then reduce Bass as total volume rises; level-match before deciding the blend is bigger.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Single notes keep edge while chords gain chest without a late, woolly low-end bloom.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The parallel channel blend changes the spectrum entering a driven non-master-volume circuit.

advanced_moves.setup: Double-track a riff with identical amp settings but different channel balances.
advanced_moves.action: Favor bright on one take and normal on the other, use the same cabinet, and vary mic position slightly rather than adding more gain.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A wide stereo pair whose center remains solid when summed to mono.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The tracks share compression and harmonic family while their spectral emphasis differs before distortion.

insider_note: The source amp is Marshall's own 1967 museum reference. The producer's secret is still basic gain staging: adding low end after the nonlinear stage is usually clearer than feeding excessive normal-channel bass into it.
avoid_when: Avoid Plexi when you need repeatable high gain at modest virtual master level or very tight stops; JMP 2203 or ENGL is easier. Choose Bluesbreaker for softer combo bloom and guitar-volume cleanup.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Marshall Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Hard rock, use complementary bright/normal blends at moderate gain, reserving the densest setting for a center overdub.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Plexi creates width through channel interaction without the preamp grain of JMP.

use_cases.application: In Stoner rock, use more normal channel but reduce Bass into the driven stage, then restore body with a darker cabinet edge position.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The power-stage harmonics create mass while cabinet choice restores lows more cleanly than overdriving bass in the amp.

name: Marshall JMP 2203
comparative_edge: Choose JMP over Plexi when focused preamp gain, tighter attack, and a master-volume workflow fit the arrangement; choose Silver Jubilee for smoother, more saturated sustain. JMP is the most direct Marshall here for lean, percussive rhythm guitars.

advanced_moves.setup: Classic master-volume Marshall move — make two states with the same perceived distortion amount but opposite Pre-Amp/Master balances.
advanced_moves.action: Use high Pre-Amp/low Master for one and lower Pre-Amp/higher Master for the other, then level-match before touching EQ.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The first is tighter and more immediate; the second is looser with more vintage power-stage movement.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The documented Pre-Amp/Master relationship shifts where distortion occurs, not merely its volume.

advanced_moves.setup: Place TUBE Overdrive before JMP for a modernized version of the amp.
advanced_moves.action: Use low pedal Drive, raise Level, reduce JMP Pre-Amp until string separation returns, and revisit Presence after setting Master.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Extra urgency without the fizzy edge of simply maxing preamp gain.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The pedal focuses the spectrum before clipping while the lower preamp setting reduces accumulated compression.

insider_note: Softube notes that the tone stack behaves differently at different Master settings. Therefore EQ decisions made before selecting the Pre-Amp/Master balance are provisional; the gain architecture must come first.
avoid_when: Avoid it for deep modern low-end mass or very smooth lead sustain; Mainstayer and Silver Jubilee are better fits. For non-master-volume bloom and channel blending, use Plexi.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Marshall Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Punk rock, use medium Pre-Amp, enough Master for body, and let picking create aggression instead of saturating every transient.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its focused upper mids keep fast consonants readable better than Mainstayer's larger lows.

use_cases.application: In Post-punk, run cleaner with higher Master, reduce Bass, and use a short room rather than a large cabinet blend.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: JMP's lean master-volume voice gives notes a hard outline without Top Boost's chime compression.

pairings.goal: Modernize JMP attack while retaining its focused Marshall midrange.
pairings.order: TUBE Overdrive → Marshall JMP 2203
pairings.setup: Use low pedal Drive/high Level, then lower JMP Pre-Amp and set Master before revisiting Presence.
pairings.why_it_works: Pre-emphasis tightens the signal before clipping while reduced preamp gain preserves more string separation.
pairings.caution: The combination can become aggressively mid-forward; do not use it automatically on already thin guitars.

name: Marshall Silver Jubilee 2555
comparative_edge: Choose Jubilee over JMP for darker, smoother saturation, wider tone-control range, and singing sustain. Choose JMP when percussive preamp bite is the priority, or Mainstayer when the lead needs American low-frequency scale rather than British mid focus.

advanced_moves.setup: Level-match pentode and triode states in the same preamp mode.
advanced_moves.action: Keep gain and cabinet fixed, switch power operation, and compensate output externally rather than with amp controls.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Triode yields a silkier, less aggressive power-stage envelope; pentode keeps more punch and authority.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The switch changes power-tube operation and modeled output behavior, not just level.

advanced_moves.setup: Use Lead mode for sustain but keep gain below the solo target.
advanced_moves.action: Add a short stereo delay after the amp, then raise gain only until bends hold through the delay gap; use the wide EQ to remove masking rather than adding more saturation.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A lead that remains vocal and sustained without turning the pick attack into fizz.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Delay supplies perceived length while the smoother preamp retains articulation at lower gain.

insider_note: Triode mode halves the modeled power output and makes power-stage distortion silkier. Level-match it externally: otherwise quieter triode can be rejected for level before its smoother envelope is judged.
avoid_when: Avoid Jubilee when hard, dry attack or vintage non-master-volume complexity is the main requirement; JMP or Plexi will speak more directly. For pristine clean headroom, use Pacific or Custom.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Marshall Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Arena rock, use Lead mode, triode for smoother power feel, and a short post-amp stereo delay with restrained feedback.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Jubilee supplies British mid sustain without Mainstayer's larger low-end footprint.

use_cases.application: In Alternative metal, use Rhythm mode in pentode, moderate gain, and the wider EQ to carve room around vocal and snare.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its mode and EQ range bridge rhythm focus and lead smoothness more flexibly than the single-channel JMP.

pairings.goal: Extend lead sustain and width without obtaining all of the note length from extra amp gain.
pairings.order: Marshall Silver Jubilee 2555 → Stereo Delay
pairings.setup: Use Lead mode at moderate gain, add a short filtered stereo delay with restrained feedback, and raise gain only until bends bridge the delay gap.
pairings.why_it_works: Jubilee supplies smooth mid sustain while delay adds perceived duration after the nonlinear amp stage.
pairings.caution: Keep the delay center and feedback controlled so repeats do not turn the already smooth lead into an indistinct wash.

name: Marshall Murder One Lemmy Signature
comparative_edge: Choose Murder One over V8 or Supernova when distorted bass must occupy the rhythm-guitar register with unmistakable upper-mid authority. Its modified Super Bass/Lead hybrid and captured 4x12 plus oversized 4x15 rig are a complete production voice, not a generic bass amp.

advanced_moves.setup: Patch and blend the brighter Volume I and darker Volume II channels before the cabinets.
advanced_moves.action: Build enough Volume II for body, add Volume I until pick and growl clear the guitars, then reduce amp Bass before compensating at the cabinet mixer.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The bass reads as a musical riff without covering the kick's deepest octave.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Channel blending shapes the spectrum before the amp's shared nonlinear stages.

advanced_moves.setup: Use the 4x12 and 4x15 as different roles rather than an equal blend.
advanced_moves.action: Choose a mid-forward dynamic mic on the 4x12, a fuller mic on the 4x15, check phase, and bring the 4x15 up only until sustained notes stop thinning.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The 4x12 defines attack and growl while the 4x15 extends weight without smearing it.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The two captured cabinets and independent mic/mixer controls let attack and body be balanced at the source.

insider_note: Long-time Motörhead producer Cameron Webb chose only nearfield dynamic microphones for the capture. The practical lesson is that the signature sound is direct and mid-forward; adding distant room too early moves away from the documented rig.
avoid_when: Avoid it for invisible clean sub support, modern slap detail, or soft vintage tube leveling; Eden, the Bass Suite DI, or V8 is more suitable. Do not expect it to leave much upper-mid room without deliberate arrangement carving.

sources.title: Softube Marshall Murder One Lemmy Signature user manual

use_cases.application: In Speed metal, favor Volume I and the 4x12, add just enough 4x15 for note length, and keep a clean sub DI below the amp lane.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its bright hybrid circuit makes bass function as a third rhythm guitar without losing Marshall identity.

use_cases.application: In Industrial rock, drive both channels, pan the two cabinets narrowly apart, and automate the 4x15 level into transitions.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The personal dual-cab rig creates arrangement-scale weight that a single generic amp layer cannot.

pairings.goal: Combine Murder One’s upper-mid grind with a controlled clean low-frequency anchor.
pairings.order: Parallel: Amp Room Bass Suite DI || Murder One amp/cab path
pairings.setup: Let the DI own the deepest octave, high-pass the Murder One lane, align phase, and balance its 4x12 for attack against the 4x15 for note length.
pairings.why_it_works: The clean DI preserves kick-compatible fundamentals while the signature rig behaves like an additional rhythm-guitar layer.
pairings.caution: Do not let the 4x15 and DI both dominate the same lows; assign one foundation and use the other for character.

name: Marshall Cabinet Collection
comparative_edge: Choose it over Celestion Speaker Shaper when real licensed Marshall cabinet identities and fast movable-mic decisions matter more than designing hypothetical speakers. Choose it over fixed IR browsing when you need continuous mic placement and controlled parallel combinations inside Amp Room.

advanced_moves.setup: Hold the amp and one microphone fixed while auditioning cabinets.
advanced_moves.action: Choose the cabinet on low-mid resonance first, then move the mic for attack; do not change cab, mic type, position, and EQ in the same pass.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The guitar occupies its arrangement octave before any finishing EQ.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Cabinet construction sets the broad resonance while mic position shapes the recorded high-frequency perspective.

advanced_moves.setup: Place two cabinets in parallel for complementary roles.
advanced_moves.action: Use a smaller/open or brighter cabinet for attack and a larger/closed cabinet for body, select dissimilar microphones, then phase-align and start the second cab 10-15 dB below the first.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The second path fills a missing region rather than merely making the rig louder.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Asymmetric level and construction prevent two full-range cabinet paths from averaging into comb-filtered sameness.

insider_note: Engineering inference from the documented seven-mic movable system: pick cabinet with one neutral mic before doing a 'mic shootout.' Otherwise the favored microphone can disguise a cabinet whose resonance is wrong for the song.
avoid_when: Avoid it when you need to alter speaker age, magnet, impedance, diameter, or breakup continuously; Celestion Speaker Shaper is the experimental tool. The collection is Amp Room-exclusive, so use native cab sections or LoadIR outside that platform.

sources.title: Softube Marshall Cabinet Collection product page

use_cases.application: In Stoner rock, pair a dark 4x12 body cab with a quieter, brighter 2x12 or 1x12 for pick outline.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Real Marshall cabinet contrasts preserve brand-coherent mids while separating fuzz density and attack.

use_cases.application: In Indie pop, use a 1x12 or 2x12 with an off-center mic rather than a 4x12, leaving bass and synth width untouched.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The collection offers smaller physical perspectives that solve scale, not just tone.

pairings.goal: Use the eight licensed Marshall cabinets as movable, parallel recording stages with any Amp Room amplifier.
pairings.order: Amp Room amplifier → one or two Marshall Cabinet Collection modules
pairings.setup: Choose one cabinet with a neutral mic first; add a second 10-15 dB lower for a missing attack or body role and phase-align before panning.
pairings.why_it_works: Amp Room provides routing, phase, and mic placement while the collection supplies historically distinct physical resonances.
pairings.caution: The collection is Amp Room-exclusive; two similar full-level cabinets often add phase problems more than useful contrast.

name: Amp Room Metal Suite
comparative_edge: Choose Metal Suite over ENGL when breadth matters more than one licensed ecosystem: it spans American Mainstayer mass, German-style articulation, wilder modern aggression, and Marshall JCM800 focus. Choose Blaze Works when only two streamlined modern voices are needed.

advanced_moves.setup: Use one cabinet and mic to compare all four suite amps from the same DI.
advanced_moves.action: Match distortion density and output, label each by envelope—loose, tight, mid-forward, or aggressive—then restore its best cabinet only after the role is chosen.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A clear reason for each amp to exist in the arrangement rather than four versions of 'more gain.'
advanced_moves.why_it_works: A controlled cabinet removes the largest downstream variable and reveals amp response.

advanced_moves.setup: Build a two-amp composite from one performance only if a single amp lacks one trait.
advanced_moves.action: Band-limit or crossover the paths, use the tighter amp for lows and a Marshall-style amp for upper mids, then align phase and print the composite before further editing.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Low strings stop cleanly while the upper-mid consonant remains human and audible.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Each amp is assigned a frequency/envelope job instead of full-range duplication.

insider_note: Controlled amp comparison is the real expert move in a suite: hold cab and mic constant first. Presets often change every stage, so they demonstrate finished rigs but do not teach which amplifier solved the problem.
avoid_when: Avoid the suite when the production needs only one historically exact amp family; ENGL or Marshall Suite provides deeper coherence. For vintage clean and edge-of-breakup work, Vintage Suite is a more efficient starting palette.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Metal Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Metalcore, use the articulated German-style amp wide and a lower-gain JCM800-family layer quietly in the center.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The suite supplies controlled modern attack and familiar British mid texture without cross-product routing.

use_cases.application: In Sludge metal, favor Mainstayer channel one with less tightening, then use a brighter secondary cabinet instead of a second amp.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its American low-end scale can remain intentionally loose while the suite's cabinet options recover articulation.

name: Amp Room Vintage Suite
comparative_edge: Choose Vintage Suite when the production needs several clean-to-crunch identities that respond differently to performance and pedals: two Pacific generations, rigid Custom 100W, and three-channel Top Boost. It is more useful than Metal Suite for roots, pop, indie, and effects-heavy arrangements.

advanced_moves.setup: Reamp one DI through all four amps with the same neutral cabinet and no pedals.
advanced_moves.action: Match output and set each just at breakup; choose by how the attack yields, then pair the selected amp with its best cabinet.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Pacific stays broad, Custom remains rigid, and Top Boost compresses through the upper mids in distinct ways.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The exercise compares dynamic architecture before familiar cabinet coloration.

advanced_moves.setup: Use one amp as a clean anchor and another only as a parallel color lane.
advanced_moves.action: Keep Pacific clean and centered; high-pass a driven Top Boost or Custom lane, pan it modestly, and automate that lane into choruses.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The chorus gains midrange energy without the clean guitar losing width or low-end stability.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Parallel roles separate foundation from harmonic emphasis while related room/mic cues keep them cohesive.

insider_note: A suite is most educational when every amp is compared through one cabinet first. This engineering-inference method reveals that the biggest choice is often transient behavior, not the familiar frequency curve supplied by the matched cab.
avoid_when: Avoid Vintage Suite for tight high gain or modern low-tuned rhythm work; Metal or ENGL is purpose-built. If the session always returns to one amp, use its separate product or Amplifiers to reduce choice overhead.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Vintage Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Indie folk, use Pacific Black barely breaking up with an off-center mic and minimal room.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its broad scoop leaves vocal and acoustic midrange intact better than Top Boost.

use_cases.application: In Post-rock, use Custom 100W for the wet foundation and a quiet Top Boost lane for section lift.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Custom preserves layered transients while Top Boost adds compressed upper-mid urgency.

name: Amp Room Bass Suite
comparative_edge: Choose Bass Suite over Eden when you need several historical and parallel personalities rather than one detailed hi-fi amp. V8 supplies tube bloom, Supernova supplies built-in clean/dirty parallelism, Cardinal supplies firm British PA-derived mids, and the suite DI anchors any of them.

advanced_moves.setup: Treat the suite DI as the low-frequency reference and choose an amp only for what the DI lacks.
advanced_moves.action: Set DI low/high cuts and Tone first, then high-pass the amp path and bring it up for sustain, growl, or pick definition; time-align before bus compression.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The combined bass remains stable when the amp lane is muted, but loses character rather than fundamental.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Assigning the DI the foundation prevents multiple full-range paths from competing for the same low-frequency job.

advanced_moves.setup: Compare V8, Supernova, and Cardinal on the same phrase through one cabinet.
advanced_moves.action: Match loudness and similar harmonic level; choose V8 for bloom, Supernova for controlled blend, or Cardinal for firm mid texture before changing cabs.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A production role, not just a preferred solo tone, becomes obvious.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Holding the cabinet constant reveals each amp's envelope and distortion structure.

insider_note: The suite's DI uses a Focusing Equalizer-inspired design. The manual's order—set low and high cuts, then Tone—is a useful secret: define the bandwidth before judging thickness, so the DI does not compete with kick or guitars by accident.
avoid_when: Avoid the suite when one pristine, highly shaped bass path is all you need; Eden WT800 is deeper and faster. For a signature distorted-bass rig rather than a flexible toolkit, Murder One is more decisive.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Bass Suite user manual

use_cases.context: Bass guitar under wide distorted guitars
use_cases.source_or_bus: Bass guitar under wide distorted guitars
use_cases.application: In Modern rock, use the DI for lows and Supernova's distorted path for center mids, aligning before a slow bus compressor.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The parallel architecture is native to Supernova and faster to balance than duplicating a conventional amp.

use_cases.application: In Psychedelic rock, keep DI/V8 fundamentals clean and automate a band-limited Cardinal path through transitions.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Cardinal's firm unusual midrange creates contrast without replacing the classic tube foundation.

name: Supernova Parallel Channel 300W
comparative_edge: Choose Supernova over V8 when the mix needs clean fundamental and dirty audibility as separate controls inside one amp, and over Eden when creative parallel distortion matters more than detailed clean EQ/bi-amping. Its strength is role separation, not vintage authenticity.

advanced_moves.setup: Start with the clean DI lane alone at the intended mix level.
advanced_moves.action: Distort the parallel channel harder than sounds polite in solo, select an EQ mode that avoids the kick fundamental, then raise it from silence until notes become readable on small speakers.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Turning the dirty lane off makes the bass recede, but leaving it on does not make the sub louder.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The clean lane restores rumble and clarity while the driven lane can be optimized only for harmonics.

advanced_moves.setup: Automate the clean/dirty balance across an arrangement.
advanced_moves.action: Keep chorus fundamentals constant, lower dirty mids in verses, and raise them before choruses rather than boosting total bass level.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The bass advances in energy without pushing the limiter or masking the kick more deeply.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Perceived loudness and audibility can rise through harmonics while low-frequency peak level stays stable.

insider_note: The expert move is to judge the dirty path from silence upward, not soloed. A distortion lane that sounds thin or ugly alone may be exactly right once the clean DI already owns the full note.
avoid_when: Avoid Supernova when you want one naturally compressing tube-amp performance with no parallel abstraction; V8 is more coherent. For surgical clean tone, crossover detail, and cabinet/direct mixing, use Eden WT800.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Bass Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Pop rock, hold the DI lane steady and ride the dirty channel into choruses for presence on guitars and phones.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its integrated parallel design changes energy without reconstructing a multi-track bass rig.

use_cases.application: In Drum and bass, use the clean lane below the kick/body crossover and aggressively distort a higher EQ mode for the drop.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Supernova provides a musician-friendly version of the clean-sub/dirty-mid split common in electronic bass design.

name: Cardinal 100W
comparative_edge: Choose Cardinal over V8 for firmer mids, clearer treble, and a less familiar British PA-derived voice; choose Supernova when you need explicit clean/dirty blending. Cardinal is a character amp for sources that need assertive mid structure more than classic bass mythology.

advanced_moves.setup: Run Cardinal as a parallel mid lane beneath a clean DI.
advanced_moves.action: High-pass above the fundamental, drive until the note gains woody density, then low-pass before cymbal range and blend quietly.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The bass remains full but becomes audible through small speakers without obvious fuzz.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Cardinal's documented firm mids and clear treble create a focused character band while the DI retains lows.

advanced_moves.setup: Try guitar through Cardinal before defaulting to a conventional guitar amp.
advanced_moves.action: Use a guitar cabinet, keep input just below heavy breakup, and hit the amp with Kraft or TUBE for section changes.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A large, dry midrange that takes pedals without the scoop of Pacific or compression of Top Boost.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Softube explicitly documents Cardinal as a sleeper guitar amp and notes its strong pedal response.

insider_note: Softube identifies the donor only as an early-'70s UK valve PA amp and recommends it for guitar too. The useful secret is to treat it as an arrangement wildcard rather than another attempt at the standard bass-amp family.
avoid_when: Avoid Cardinal for deep clean authority or immediately recognizable classic bass tone; Eden, V8, or Murder One communicates those roles faster. Its firm mids can crowd vocal and guitars unless the path is deliberately band-limited.

sources.title: Softube Amp Room Bass Suite user manual

use_cases.application: In Psychedelic rock, automate a band-limited Cardinal lane beneath a cleaner V8 or DI foundation.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its unusual firm British mids sound less canonical than the American tube-bass options.

use_cases.application: In Noise rock, use Cardinal as a relatively firm platform before fuzz, then choose a smaller cabinet to control low-end scale.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It accepts pedals while retaining an unpolished PA-like midrange that conventional guitar amps smooth over.

name: Amp Room Eden WT800 Suite
comparative_edge: Choose Eden over the Bass Suite's tube amps when clean articulation, semi-parametric shaping, controlled compression, and true bi-amp roles matter. Choose Supernova for intentionally dirty parallel mids; Eden's direct, 1x15, and 4x10 paths are about detailed record-ready balance.

advanced_moves.setup: Set input Gain so the green indicator responds normally, then leave the parametric bands flat.
advanced_moves.action: Adjust Enhance, Bass/Treble, and Compressor first; only then use the three semi-parametric bands to solve a remaining arrangement conflict.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The source feels finished before narrow EQ, and the compressor sustains without dulling attack.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Softube's recommended order separates broad amp voicing and input-dependent dynamics from surgical correction.

advanced_moves.setup: Engage Bi-Amp mode with 1x15 low and 4x10 high paths plus the post-amp direct channel.
advanced_moves.action: Sweep Crossover while listening to upper-bass note definition, choose separate mics, and bring direct level up last; watch the master clip light rather than only individual meters.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The 1x15 supplies body, the 4x10 articulates notes, and direct signal restores immediacy without phase hollowness.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The crossover assigns physical cabinet roles before their independent channel-strip blend.

insider_note: Input Gain changes how much the one-knob compressor works. That means gain staging is part of the compression setting; changing input later requires rechecking sustain and attack even if the Compressor knob did not move.
avoid_when: Avoid Eden when vintage tube bloom, obvious grit, or a one-control clean/dirty parallel concept is the point; V8 and Supernova are faster. Eden can be needless complexity for a bass part already correct at the DI.

use_cases.application: In Gospel, use moderate Enhance, light input-aware compression, and Bi-Amp crossover for clear low-B fundamentals and fast upper runs.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Eden offers more deliberate clean articulation and cabinet division than the vintage tube choices.

use_cases.application: In Electronic pop, run the stereo instance, use the direct channel for center stability, and keep cabinet blend modest for physical midrange.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The plug-in processes stereo channels independently and Softube explicitly recommends it beyond bass guitar.

name: Celestion Speaker Shaper
comparative_edge: Choose Speaker Shaper over Marshall Cabinet Collection or static IRs when the question is why a speaker works: age, breakup, diameter, magnet, impedance, cabinet back, and count can be varied continuously. Choose the licensed cabinets when believable fixed hardware identity and faster decisions matter more.

advanced_moves.setup: Start from a real Celestion speaker with default physical values and one microphone.
advanced_moves.action: Choose open/closed back and speaker count first, then diameter; next compare New/Run-in and add only enough Speaker Distortion to change touch. Leave magnet experiments until the physical cabinet scale works.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The low-mid resonance fits the arrangement before top-end mic or EQ decisions.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Cabinet geometry and speaker scale make larger structural changes than fine material parameters.

advanced_moves.setup: Use two microphones in Realistic phase mode.
advanced_moves.action: Make one the anchor, move the second from center toward edge and vary distance, then switch only the pair to Aligned for comparison at equal output.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Realistic phase may create useful contour; Aligned should sound more stable and direct rather than automatically better.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The model preserves distance-related phase until automatic alignment is enabled.

insider_note: The Amp Room module is not identical to the native plug-in: it exposes one speaker instead of two and removes the native room section. Add a parallel second module and RoomIR when those omissions matter.
avoid_when: Avoid it when fast, historically recognizable cabinet choices are the priority; Marshall Cabinet Collection or a suite's matched cabs are more decisive. Extreme hypothetical settings should be framed as sound design, not as models of existing hardware.

sources.title: Softube Celestion Speaker Shaper user manual

use_cases.context: One amp reused across verse and chorus
use_cases.source_or_bus: One amp reused across verse and chorus
use_cases.application: In Alternative rock, automate from smaller/run-in/open-back behavior in verses toward larger/closed/newer and slightly more breakup in choruses.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Continuous speaker variables change perceived rig scale without switching the amplifier performance.

use_cases.application: In Experimental bass music, try physically impossible large diameters or magnet combinations on a high-passed lane, keeping sub dry.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its Celestion-verified 'what-if' model can create speaker behavior no fixed IR library contains.

pairings.goal: Place algorithmic speaker design inside a complete pedal/amp/parallel-routing environment.
pairings.order: Amp Room amp with cabinet bypassed → Celestion Speaker Shaper module → RoomIR/post effects
pairings.setup: Set Amp Room gain first, build one realistic speaker/cab state, then use Speaker Shaper’s physical variables for the missing scale or breakup.
pairings.why_it_works: The processors divide the rig at the same boundary as hardware: amplifier behavior first, speaker/capture behavior second.
pairings.caution: The Amp Room module omits the native room and second speaker; add them explicitly rather than assuming preset parity.

name: Acoustic Feedback
comparative_edge: Choose Acoustic Feedback over pitch shifting, distortion sustain, or a feedback sample when the harmonic must emerge from the played note and follow bends. It is a performance processor before the amp, not a generic post-amp special effect.

advanced_moves.setup: Use a high-impedance DI, healthy input peaks, Acoustic Feedback first, and the amp simulator after it.
advanced_moves.action: Start controls near noon, hold one note, and set Feedback for a natural buildup time; then raise Tolerance only enough that bends and vibrato retain the feedback.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The harmonic arrives after the dry note and remains connected to expressive movement rather than snapping on instantly.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Feedback controls loop growth while Tolerance relaxes how strictly the model follows the source's changing conditions.

advanced_moves.setup: Print a dedicated feedback performance rather than leaving the processor live on every phrase.
advanced_moves.action: Automate Feedback upward on selected held notes, perform bends into the harmonic, record several passes, and comp only the transitions that behave musically.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Feedback sounds like an intentional performance event, not a uniform sustain plug-in.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The model depends on pitch, pickup, input level, and playing, so performance curation exploits rather than fights its variability.

insider_note: Softube recommends placing the amp simulator after Acoustic Feedback. Reversing the order deprives the model of its intended instrument-to-amp loop behavior; the 'secret' is correct physical ordering and a well-leveled DI, not an extreme Feedback setting.
avoid_when: Avoid it on already printed full mixes or sources where exact repeatability is required. Use a pitch shifter or resampled feedback effect when every trigger must be identical, and avoid Wild settings if naturalism is the goal.

use_cases.context: Held guitar notes between chord walls
use_cases.source_or_bus: Held guitar notes between chord walls
use_cases.application: In Shoegaze, print feedback swells before the main reverb and edit them into gaps, leaving rhythm chords untreated.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The harmonic grows from the actual guitar pitch and survives bends more organically than a generated octave layer.

use_cases.application: In Art rock, use Natural Feedback with moderate Tolerance and perform slow position-like harmonic changes through bends and vibrato.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its modeled loop recreates the responsive studio-feedback gesture without loud monitor placement.

pairings.goal: Generate note-following feedback from the clean guitar signal before it enters the modeled amplifier and cabinet.
pairings.order: Acoustic Feedback → Amp Room
pairings.setup: Use a high-impedance DI, set natural buildup and moderate Tolerance on held notes, then choose the Amp Room rig after feedback behavior is stable.
pairings.why_it_works: Acoustic Feedback models the instrument-to-amplifier loop and expects the amp simulator after it, matching the physical signal relationship.
pairings.caution: Input level, pickup, pitch, and playing change the result; print selected performances rather than expecting identical triggers.

name: Softube Flow Complete Suite
comparative_edge: Choose Complete over Flow Mixing when Model Series instruments and the Mastering environment are recurring parts of the same workflow; choose Flow Mastering alone when finalization is the only gap. The value is not merely the 100+ roster—it is moving from guided macro chains into the exact underlying Softube processors without changing ecosystems.

advanced_moves.setup: Open a factory Flow that gets near the target, then reveal the underlying chain before committing.
advanced_moves.action: Bypass one module at a time, note which Flow Control moves which audible job, and remove any stage that contributes only level. Save the lean result as a User Signal Chain.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Each remaining stage has a named job and bypass no longer produces a hidden loudness penalty.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Factory macros can move several processors at once; decomposing the chain turns a preset into a repeatable production method.

advanced_moves.setup: Build a project palette before browsing the full subscription roster.
advanced_moves.action: Choose one corrective EQ, fast compressor, leveler, character EQ, space, saturator, amp, and two instruments; favorite them and finish a full production before adding alternates.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Faster decisions and consistent color across tracks without losing access to specialists when a real exception appears.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: A constrained default set prevents the growing catalog from turning every routine job into a shootout.

use_cases.source_or_bus: Model Series synth tracks and their mix chains
use_cases.application: Write with a Model synth, shape it in Flow Mixing, then save the instrument and Flow chain as separate presets so arrangement and processing remain independently editable.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Complete is the only Flow tier here that connects the Model instruments, Mixing, and Mastering environments under one entitlement.

use_cases.application: Keep creative bus tone in Flow Mixing, export a level-safe premaster, and open a separate Flow Mastering session rather than stacking both environments on the active mix.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The suite provides both workflows while the separate-session boundary preserves a clear mastering comparison.

insider_note: The included plug-ins load separately as VST, AU, or AAX. The useful expert move is to begin with a Flow for orientation, then replace the macro with native instances when automation, routing, or recall needs to be explicit.
avoid_when: Avoid Complete when you repeatedly use a small fixed set and do not need the Model instruments or both Flow environments; perpetual à-la-carte tools or a narrower Flow tier reduces roster and entitlement complexity.

sources.title: Softube Flow Complete Suite product page

name: Flow Mixing Suite
comparative_edge: Choose Flow Mixing over a conventional channel strip when the source needs a guided multi-effect chain, explanatory context, and a few performance-scale controls. Choose Console 1 Core Mixing Suite for repetitive channel work where direct section-by-section control is faster, or native plug-ins when complex automation must remain transparent.

advanced_moves.setup: Load a source-specific Flow with input and output level matched.
advanced_moves.action: Turn each macro through its full range while watching which modules move, return to neutral, then set only the two controls that solve the largest problems; customize the chain afterward.
advanced_moves.listen_for: A clear before/after cause rather than a generally more processed, louder result.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Macro ranges reveal the designer's intended division of labor before small settings conceal it.

advanced_moves.setup: Create a User Signal Chain for a repeat source such as lead vocal or drum bus.
advanced_moves.action: Map one-to-one controls for the parameters that change per song—threshold, de-ess amount, ambience level—not fixed setup choices such as filter topology. Name each control by audible result.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Session-to-session adjustment happens from a short surface while the stable engineering remains protected underneath.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Current user mapping is one parameter per control, so choosing variable decisions deliberately is more useful than imitating factory multi-parameter macros.

use_cases.application: Build a chain with peak control, slower leveling, dynamic harshness, and ambience; expose only peak threshold, leveler amount, harshness range, and reverb send as User Controls.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Flow keeps a multi-stage vocal method approachable while still allowing the processors to be opened and edited.

use_cases.application: Use a Flow for compression, saturation, and width on a return, then automate one output or wet control rather than moving three native processors independently.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: A controlled macro surface is especially useful when the chain is an arrangement effect rather than transparent bus maintenance.

insider_note: User Signal Chains can currently make simplified one-to-one mappings, not the full multi-parameter macros found in factory Flows. Design user controls around the decisions that truly vary, rather than trying to recreate a factory Flow authoring system.
avoid_when: Avoid Flow Mixing for a single obvious EQ or compressor move; load the native processor directly. Avoid hiding a chain behind macros when another mixer must audit every automated parameter quickly.

sources.title: Softube Flow Mixing Suite product page and FAQ

name: Flow Mastering Suite
comparative_edge: Choose Flow Mastering over individual Weiss and Chandler tools when a producer needs guided chain architecture, loudness/true-peak context, references, and macro control in one place. Choose the native Weiss tools when mastering is already a deliberate step-by-step practice and every detector, release, and delivery choice must remain exposed.

advanced_moves.setup: Load the loudest passage, set input target, and import a level-matched reference before choosing a Flow.
advanced_moves.action: Audition three Flows at matched output, select by the smallest structural correction, then reduce the main macro moves by half and rebuild only what the track proves it needs.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The master moves toward the reference's balance and density without losing the mix's own transient and depth hierarchy.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Starting from restrained, gain-compensated differences reduces the tendency to choose the loudest or most transformed chain.

advanced_moves.setup: Separate tone approval from delivery approval.
advanced_moves.action: First work with low-latency/oversampling choices held constant; after tone is approved, compare True Peak, oversampling, and dither settings on the final delivery format and save them as an export-state note.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Delivery changes do not alter the approved tonal balance or introduce intersample clipping.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Limiter mode, oversampling, and dithering answer format and reconstruction problems, not the same aesthetic question as EQ or compression.

use_cases.application: Use the gain-difference meter and bypass individual modules to determine whether a perceived improvement is tonal, dynamic, or simply louder before revising the mix.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Flow's integrated views make the chain a diagnostic surface rather than only a finishing preset.

use_cases.application: Approve the chain without dither first, then set True Peak, oversampling, and dither once for the target file format and document that export state.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The delivery controls live alongside loudness history and reference auditioning, reducing handoff errors.

insider_note: The built-in gain-difference view is the real power feature for producer mastering: it helps expose when a macro's appeal comes from level. Use it continuously, not only at the final bypass check.
avoid_when: Avoid it as a substitute for fixing an unstable mix; if every Flow needs large corrective moves, return to stems. Choose DS1-MK3/EQ1 directly when an experienced mastering engineer needs full, explicit control rather than a macro layer.

sources.title: Softube Flow Mastering Suite user manual

name: Volume 6
comparative_edge: Choose Volume 6 over Flow Complete when perpetual ownership of a large fixed snapshot matters more than a growing guided subscription. Choose a focused collection when only one family—Weiss, Tube-Tech, Empirical Labs, or compressors—will enter daily work; Volume's breadth is useful only if it is organized by job.

advanced_moves.setup: Before installing templates, inventory the collection by production role rather than brand.
advanced_moves.action: Select one default for corrective EQ, fast dynamics, leveling, bus tone, room, delay, saturation, synth, and amp; put all alternates in a secondary folder and require a stated reason to open them.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Projects develop a consistent vocabulary and specialty tools appear only when the source proves a need.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Role-based constraints convert a broad anthology into a working system instead of repeated choice paralysis.

advanced_moves.setup: Create a recall policy for the three included legacy products.
advanced_moves.action: Tag FET Compressor Mk I, Bass Amp Room, and Vintage Amp Room as recall-only, keep them out of new-session favorites, and print references before replacing them in old projects.
advanced_moves.listen_for: New work never depends on unsupported products while archived sessions remain reproducible.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Softube includes those products for compatibility, not as evidence that they are preferred current tools.

use_cases.application: Assign a small default set across templates, then create named specialty lanes such as Weiss-clean, Summit-tube, and dirty parallel instead of browsing the collection per insert.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Volume supplies enough cross-category depth to build several coherent palettes from one perpetual snapshot.

use_cases.source_or_bus: Model 84, Modular, Heartbeat, Parallels, and amp instruments
use_cases.application: Keep one instrument per synthesis role in favorites and bounce older project-critical presets before major host/OS changes.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The collection spans instruments and effects, but its fixed nature makes deliberate long-term recall more realistic than a changing subscription roster.

insider_note: Volume 6's three legacy products are explicitly present to keep existing projects safe and may be unsupported. The expert habit is to separate 'licensed for recall' from 'approved for new work' in plug-in folders and templates.
avoid_when: Avoid Volume 6 if you already own most key products or need only one specialist family; a focused collection reduces duplicates. Choose Flow if guided chains, macros, and ongoing roster additions are the primary value.

name: Softube Essentials
comparative_edge: Choose Essentials over Volume or Flow when a deliberate five-tool constraint is an advantage: Tape, British Class A, FET Compressor Mk II, Model 84, and Wasted Space. It is a production palette, not a complete mix suite; its character is stronger than its repair or delivery coverage.

advanced_moves.setup: Build a song template that assigns each included product one non-overlapping job.
advanced_moves.action: Use British Class A for channel shaping, FET for peak envelope, Tape for shared cohesion, Wasted Space only as an effect return, and Model 84 as the instrument source; do not stack them by default.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Each processor remains identifiable and the mix avoids accumulated analog color on every path.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Distinct job assignment prevents a small collection from becoming one repeated 'vintage' chain.

advanced_moves.setup: Run a five-tool finish challenge on one production, allowing stock utility processors for missing repair tasks.
advanced_moves.action: Complete the mix before adding any specialist Softube product, document what the five tools genuinely could not solve, and expand only for those proven gaps.
advanced_moves.listen_for: New purchases or additions correspond to recurring production problems rather than curiosity.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: A constrained palette reveals whether the missing need is corrective, spatial, dynamic, or delivery-specific.

use_cases.application: Keep Model 84 mostly unprocessed at first, use FET only for envelope emphasis, then send selected parts to Wasted Space rather than inserting it everywhere.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The five-product set creates a coherent '80s-to-modern character path without requiring the full catalog.

use_cases.application: Use British Class A on individual problem groups and one restrained Tape instance on a shared bus, keeping FET for tracks that need actual peak control.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The collection's three mix processors cover complementary color/envelope roles when they are not reflexively stacked.

insider_note: The collection omits a modern corrective EQ, transparent limiter, and general-purpose clean reverb. Treating those omissions as intentional boundaries—and using stock utilities where needed—is more productive than forcing character tools into unsuitable roles.
avoid_when: Avoid Essentials if the goal is a self-contained mastering, surgical mixing, or broad guitar toolkit. Use a focused specialist collection or Flow tier rather than assuming 'Essentials' means every necessary production category.

pairings.goal: Use British Class A for local channel tone and Tape for shared bus cohesion without stacking both heavily on every track.
pairings.order: British Class A on selected channels/subgroups → one restrained Tape stage on the shared bus
pairings.setup: Commit channel EQ/dynamics first, drive Tape at matched output on the group or mix bus, and bypass individual tape stages unless they solve a distinct source problem.
pairings.why_it_works: The console strip shapes local sources while the shared tape stage applies common nonlinear compression and spectral glue.
pairings.caution: Repeated high-drive console and tape stages can darken transients and accumulate low-mid density.

name: Icons Compressor Collection
comparative_edge: Choose Icons when the recurring decision is envelope family rather than brand mythology: fast FET, slow opto, or hard-knee VCA. Choose Bus Processor, 670, or CL 1B when bus architecture, vari-mu bloom, or adjustable Tube-Tech leveling is the actual requirement.

advanced_moves.setup: Insert all three on the same source with Drive off, Dry/Wet at 100%, and matched output.
advanced_moves.action: Aim for similar peak reduction, then adjust attack/release only enough to expose each design's natural behavior; compare in context before adding Drive or parallel blend.
advanced_moves.listen_for: FET controls the front edge, OPTO reshapes level over time, and VCA adds a compact hard-knee event.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Removing modern extras reveals the detector and gain-reduction envelope that should decide the choice.

advanced_moves.setup: Build a two-stage vocal chain with FET before OPTO.
advanced_moves.action: Let FET catch only the quickest peaks, then set OPTO for 1-3 dB of slower leveling; level-match each stage and use sidechain filtering before increasing compression.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The vocal stays forward without either compressor audibly working hard.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Peak containment gives the slower opto a narrower input range, allowing it to level rather than chase transients.

use_cases.application: Use FET for fast peaks and OPTO for slow body, keeping each stage modest and using HF make-up only after compression is approved.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The collection supplies complementary envelopes in matched modern interfaces, making serial division of labor easy to hear.

use_cases.application: Drive VCA or FET harder on a return, compare hard-knee snap against all-buttons-style density, then blend below the dry bus.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The VCA/FET contrast offers two distinct kinds of aggression without moving to unrelated processing families.

insider_note: The modern panels are deliberately similar, so hide or neutralize Drive, HF make-up, sidechain, and Dry/Wet during the first comparison. Otherwise shared extras can disguise the one thing worth learning: how each gain-reduction element shapes time.
avoid_when: Avoid the set for transparent mastering dynamics or full mix-bus architecture; Weiss and Bus Processor are more appropriate. Do not choose OPTO for truly instant peak containment or FET when slow, invisible leveling is the goal.

sources.title: Softube Icons: The Compressor Collection product page

pairings.partner: FET Compressor Mk II + OPTO Compressor
pairings.goal: Use fast peak control before slower musical leveling on a vocal.
pairings.order: FET Compressor Mk II → OPTO Compressor
pairings.setup: Let FET catch only the quickest peaks, then ask OPTO for a few dB of slower level control; match gain after each stage.
pairings.why_it_works: The first stage narrows the vocal’s peak range so the slower opto can control body without chasing every consonant.
pairings.caution: Two compressors can hide over-processing; bypass each independently and do not let both produce large continuous reduction.

name: Weiss Complete Collection 3
comparative_edge: Choose the Weiss collection when transparent digital mastering and post work recur often enough to justify both deep code ports and faster derivatives. Use DS1-MK3, DS5, or EQ1 for unusual or high-stakes problems; use MM-1, Deess, EQ MP, and Compressor/Limiter when the job is narrow and speed matters.

advanced_moves.setup: For every task, begin with the narrowest Weiss derivative that plausibly solves it.
advanced_moves.action: Move to the parent processor only when a missing detector, filter, timing, or channel mode blocks the result; save the reason in the preset name.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Faster recall and fewer irrelevant controls without giving up access to deep architecture when evidence demands it.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Several focused plug-ins derive algorithms from the larger Weiss processors, so depth can be chosen by task rather than sonic prestige.

advanced_moves.setup: Create a clean-master shootout between DS1-MK3 and the focused Compressor/Limiter or MM-1.
